The damage would be greater caused by the shockwave because water is more dense so the energy is carried harder. The speed of sound in water is about 1,482 metres per second but in air it's just 332 metres per second - so sound/pressure waves are almost four times more powerful in water. However, if you lie flat and close to the surface of the water, you can almost escape entirely the effects.
answers.qualifications: Saw it tested on Mythbusters

questions.question: What is deja vu? How is it that you feel like you've done something before? It's such a strong feeling that you've been in that exact position before.

answers.answer: Deja vu is effectively a very minor seizure. The electrical impulses controlling your sensory input are being sent to the wrong part of the brain for a second. Although you're experiencing the present, it goes to the part of the brain associated with memory, so you sense it as a memory. Some people feel slightly disoriented. The brain is just doing a little funny rewiring.
answers.qualifications: Asked his uncle who is a neurosurgeon in Chicago

questions.question: How do they put cranes up? You need another crane to put up a crane, but then you need another crane to put up that crane... How does it start?

answers.answer: You can build it at ground level and then hoist it up with a portable crane.

questions.question: Why are the speeds on old record players 33, 45 and 78? 33 plus 45 equals 78 - is this just a coincidence or is there a technical reason for this mathematical relationship?
Why is blowing a raspberry called a raspberry? What is the origin of the term?

answers.caller: Paul the Ice Cream Man from Greys
answers.answer: It comes from the 2 Ronnies sketch with Charlie Farley and the Phantom, where 'raspberry tart' was rhyming slang for something rude. Blowing a raspberry = raspberry tart.

questions.question: How can you donate your body to become a classroom skeleton like the ones in Belgian schools?

answers.answer: Due to the Human Tissue Act following the Alder Hey scandal, institutions must have HTA officers who are personally responsible. Anatomy schools need cadavers for dissection. You can make a codicil in your will to donate your body to medical science. After dissection, remains are buried with respect. Skeletons for teaching are now usually fiberglass.

questions.question: What are those structures that look like small roofs on poles, sometimes green or yellow, with numbers in France?

answers.answer: They are markers for underground fuel lines - gas, oil, or aviation fuel pipelines. Especially near major fuel plants like the Isle of Grain. They are inspected periodically.

questions.question: Why do cigarette butts have that orange and yellow pattern on the filter?

answers.answer: They were originally patented as 'corkies' - filters made of cork. When technology advanced and they moved to modern filters, they kept the cork pattern so customers wouldn't be spooked by the change. It became a standard design.

questions.caller: Paul the Ice Cream Man from Greys
questions.question: Why is a lolly stuck in an ice cream called a Popeye?

answers.answer: Lollipop + Ice cream = Popeye. Lolly = Lollipop, Ice cream = 'ice' with 'pop' - combine them and you get Popeye.

Ice cream men used to say 'mind your eye on the stick' (of the lollipop). It could have been called Popeye or 'eye popper' because of the danger to eyes when kids hold them with the stick pointing up.

questions.question: When I wash a red T-shirt with white T-shirts and the dye runs, why doesn't the dye come out of the whites when I wash them again?

answers.answer: The dye in the red T-shirt isn't completely absorbed by the fiber, so some washes out. That's why red clothes fade, but they never fade to white. The fiber holds the dye in a way that can never be fully removed without bleach.

questions.question: How fast does the data travel when I order something online and get an instant confirmation text back?

answers.answer: The electrical signal travels at about 66% of the speed of light, and the electromagnetic signal (like Wi-Fi/text) travels at the speed of light - approximately 186,000 miles per second.

questions.question: Why do chickens lay eggs all year round while wild birds only lay during breeding seasons?

answers.answer: The statement may not be entirely correct. Many common utility birds in Britain are bred to hatch eggs most of the year round. Hobbyist breeds don't lay eggs all year. So it's not all chickens that lay year-round.

questions.question: How come the Queen has two birthdays?

answers.answer: The actual calendar birthday is only relevant to the current monarch. The official birthday applies to all monarchs so it can be planned in advance - you can close traffic, invite foreign heads of state, etc. If the monarch died the day before their actual birthday, the celebration could still go ahead under the new monarch.

A previous king had his birthday in winter and wanted to celebrate but the weather was atrocious. So he moved his birthday to summer months for better weather. The official birthday ensures everyone can be invited in advance regardless of who is monarch.

questions.question: Since finishing a strong course of antibiotics for pneumonia, why has my sweat smelled permanently different - a sweet smell?
Why do you get that horrible feeling when you scrape your nails along a chalkboard or tiles?

answers.answer: It's evolutionary psychology. Human beings are most sensitive to the human scream - it gives us survival benefit. The human scream is roughly the same frequency as scraping your nails down a blackboard. When one of your family or tribe was being eaten by a predator they'd scream at practically that frequency. That's why when we hear that frequency coming out of a blackboard we shiver - it's the resonant frequency of a human ear.

questions.question: Why is there nobody called cobbler?

answers.answer: By the time the word cobbler became into common parlance we'd stopped naming people after their livelihood. When we were still naming people after their occupation, they were still called shoemakers. The most common occupation of people in the French Revolution were cobblers.

questions.question: Why are dusters yellow?

answers.answer: The Knights Hospitular in Malta (Knights of St John) when they were tending people with contagious diseases wore a long yellow shift to sort of colourably around them - everything had to be kept clean and washed afterwards, so yellow becomes associated with cleanliness and that's why dusters are yellow.

In the old days when everything was brought in by boat and they had all major diseases on the boats, they used to pull up different coloured flags. If it was a yellow flag it meant the boat was free of disease and could come straight into port. That's why dusters are yellow.
This was on Mystery Hour a couple of years ago. (Confirming Natalie's answer as correct - also in the duster business)

questions.question: Can you yawn and sneeze at the same time?
Can stress actually send you grey? Can it give you grey hair?
Where are tears stored? When you're not crying, where are they waiting?

answers.answer: Tears come from lacrimal glands - they don't just come when you cry. Your eyes are always wet and when you blink you're spreading tears. They contain disinfectants and lysosomes. When you cry, the rate of production accelerates. There is a kind of reservoir in the lacrimal glands - you can run out of tears if you cry for a long time. With onions, it's a chemical irritant and the body floods your eye with water to dilute the irritants.

questions.question: Are there swear words in every single language?

answers.answer: I was in an international school overseas when I was a kid. At one point I could pretty much swear in 52 different languages.

In Nigeria there are no swear words. There are three main languages - Ibo, Hausa, and Yoruba - and none of them contain rude words. If they want to abuse someone they borrow words from the West and add them into the language.

questions.question: When you lose your sight you're blind, when you lose your hearing you're deaf - is there any words for the loss of the other three senses (touch, smell, taste)?
Elvis was famous for curling his top lip. Why can you only curl your top lip to the left and not to the right?

answers.answer: I can move it to the right. (Overturning the premise of the question - claiming he CAN curl to the right)

questions.question: Why do professional tennis players accept three balls, inspect them, throw one away, put one in their pocket, and serve with the third one? Why do they keep one in their pocket?

answers.answer: It's the rules - they have to keep the second ball in their pocket so that they can't waste time in between the first serve and second serve and distract their opponent. It helps maintain rhythm.

questions.question: Why is it called a 'Popeye' when you put a lolly in ice cream?
How do water features with large metal bowls work, where water comes up through the top, runs down the side, and at the halfway point doesn't fall off but clings and goes around the bowl?

answers.answer: It's about water tension/meniscus. The water molecules cling to themselves at a certain flow rate. You need to keep the flow low, and then the water will cling and only come off at the bottom when it flows back into the pond. The meniscus on the water holds the water to the ball. Gravity will overcome that at certain speeds. I have a degree in human biology where we learned about surfactants and water tension.

questions.question: Why do most houses have front doors that open inwards? Wouldn't it be better for security if they opened outwards?

answers.answer: Using a thought experiment: if your door opened outwards and you were rushing out late for work, you'd hit anyone standing outside - e.g., someone just coming to borrow milk, concussing them. Outward opening doors could be a security risk.
With UPVC doors, if you open inwards, the hinges are inside so they're safer. If you open outwards, hinges are on the outside and can be attacked or ground off.

There's also something about servants for inside doors so when dressing, the door would be in the way and you'd have warning when a servant came with your bedpan while you were in your bloomers. But that doesn't work for front doors.

questions.question: Why don't you get hungover when you're younger? My 16-year-old brother is fine every Sunday morning, playing football, while at 20 I'm comatose.

answers.answer: At 20, you're on the nursery slopes of hangovers. 20-year-olds don't know they're born when it comes to hangovers. It gets MUCH worse. James was still drinking at 26, but hangovers later lasted weeks.

questions.question: If I bumped into someone in Gatwick in 54 BC and asked what year it was, what would they say? How did they calculate time before Christ, before standardized calendars?

answers.answer: The Romans had conquered that part of Britain by 54 BC, so you'd probably be under the Roman calendar. Further north, the indigenous Celtic population would be following their own Celtic calendar. So in Gatwick, you'd likely be using the Roman calendar. The Romans dated from the notional founding of Rome, 750 BC. So 750 minus 54 = year 696.

The Romans didn't invade to stay until after 54 BC. So you couldn't have had a Roman date at that time. If you were in Gatwick, there would have been a local tribe - the Regnii. You'd date by how long the local warlord had been in power, like the 17th year of the reign of the local chieftain. We didn't start using AD until around 600 AD.

questions.question: Why does my Springer Spaniel come to me whenever I sneeze, even if he's asleep or in another room? Other dog owners say their dogs do the same thing. Is it the noise? There's been no training involved.

answers.answer: He's obviously worried about you. Dogs can perceive things about humans. Could be he's picked up on you being poorly.

questions.question: Do colored contact lenses restrict your vision like sunglasses? Specifically, the solid colored ones like Marilyn Manson wears where the pupil appears fixed. If you walked into a dark room and your pupil wanted to dilate, would that be a problem?

answers.answer: Mrs O'Brien got solid red witch's eyes for Halloween and she could see absolutely normally even through the solid red. She didn't see the world as red.
I'll review this position if anyone challenges it, but I think the colored ones that are clear would be like sunglasses, but the solid colored ones still let you see normally.

questions.question: On a nice sunny day, you see a cast or shadow of quite a large size passing by - not a cloud, not a bird, not a plane, nothing visible in the sky that could have caused such a shadow. What's causing it?

answers.answer: I have no idea what you're talking about. If there's a shadow, something caused it. It could be a plane, or a building, or a cloud that's too high up to see.

questions.question: I get static electricity shocks from my car all the time, and it happens with other vehicles too. Even when I change clothes and shoes, I still get shocked while my friends don't. I've had the car checked and garages say nothing is wrong. My friends don't experience this. Why is this happening to me? How can I stop it?

answers.answer: There's a bad earth in the vehicle - when touching mechanical metal parts you're making ground contact and getting shocked every time.

When Zen gets out of the car, he puts one foot outside and slides across the seat, which generates the static. Then when he touches the key or outside of the car, he transfers the charge back to the car. The solution is to touch the metal part of the door as he slides across the seat so the charge transfers straight into the car slowly rather than building up. Don't slide and charge - touch the metal body.
Drive naked. Wear some pants so you don't get arrested. Then see if it happens with no clothes on. You need an all-over body lotion. Keep an outfit in the back of your car.

questions.question: What is the origin of the term 'tea towel'? Why are they called tea towels when tea doesn't seem to have anything to do with them?

answers.answer: From Victorian times, the mistress of the household had a separate towel just to clean the silver tea set with. No one else could touch it. It's carried on from there and become the tea towel.

questions.question: What happens to Japanese snow monkeys when they get out of hot springs? They get wet, it's freezing cold in the snow, so how do they stay warm? If it's about fur, why did they need the hot spring in the first place?

answers.answer: When they get out of the hot water, they shake themselves and all the water comes off their fur. That's how they keep warm. I saw it on a BBC programme.

questions.question: Why do hangovers get worse as you get older?

answers.answer: Scientifically, hangovers don't get worse with age.
Every single person listening knows that they DO get worse. I'm afraid you're wrong.

questions.question: Why do pencils have labels like H, B, F, 2B, 3B, etc.? What do these letters mean and where does the random F come from?

answers.answer: H stands for hard, B stands for black. HB is a middling pencil. When it goes to H, it becomes harder with less graphite. F probably stands for fairly hard.

H means hard and B means black. The pencil lead is made of carbon graphite. The higher the H number, the more graphite and the lighter the stroke. F denotes a fine hard pencil that can be sharpened to a very sharp point. The B pencils have more carbon and give darker, softer strokes as you go up the B scale.

questions.question: Why don't we dream with sound, smell or touch? Why is it just visual?

answers.answer: Conducted informal poll of studio crew. Three out of four reported hearing sounds in dreams. Acknowledged it may be primarily visual for some people but not exclusively.
He is now blind. When sighted, dreams were visual. Now blind, dreams have no visual element but sound and speech remain. No smell in his dreams.

questions.question: Why when you're on the bottom of the planet doesn't it feel like you're upside down?

answers.answer: Acknowledged it was a good question needing someone cleverer to explain. Suggested gravity is the answer.

There's no top or bottom of the planet. In space, there's no up and down. Gravity pulls you in a direct line between the centre of the Earth and you. Wherever your feet point toward the centre of the Earth, that is your down. People in Australia feel exactly the same as we do because we're both being pulled toward the centre of the Earth. Examples: motorcyclist on wall of death feels upright; roller coaster riders feel up at the top of loops.

questions.question: What defines limited edition? Who defines it?

answers.answer: A limited edition has a finite number. Once that limit is reached, no more can be made under that designation - you could sue if they did. It's about value and exclusivity. If a Dennis the Menace print was limited to 500, it's worth more than if 5 million were printed.

questions.question: Why do two pieces of chicken from the same box have different instructions - one says 'defrost thoroughly' and one says 'cooked from frozen'?
Why doesn't sea salt smell of the ocean when everything else from the sea (seaweed, fish, shells) does?

answers.answer: Suggested it's the water - salt has come a long way from the sea while other items are still covered in seawater.
Salt only smells when water is introduced to it. Standing by the sea you smell it because water is being blown in. When it dries out in summer, you don't smell it at all.

questions.question: If you boil a batch of eggs all from the same box, why do some peel easily in one piece while others peel in little bits?
Why do cats respond to kissing sounds (come over when you kiss at them) but dogs don't, while dogs respond to whistles but cats don't?
Why does hearing certain musical notes (like Sam Smith singing) give you shivers and goosebumps? I understand goosebumps from temperature but why from sound?

answers.answer: Anthony and the Johnsons give her genuine shivers down her spine.
Suggested it might be emotional rather than frequency - mentioned minor key music gives him goosebumps.

questions.question: Why do we have to put our phones in airplane/flight mode on a plane? What happens if you don't?

answers.answer: Stops the phone trying to send out signals that might interfere with aircraft. Electromagnetic radiation from phones is the concern. Modern planes now offer Wi-Fi while phones are in airplane mode.

questions.question: Why are eggs in the same box so different? Why do some peel easily and others don't?

answers.answer: Eggs come from different farms and different chickens by the time they reach you. The peelability depends on the age of the egg - the shell is porous and lets in air. Older eggs have more air inside, making them easier to peel. Fresh eggs (like from a farm) are very hard to peel. Fresh eggs also poach better. If an egg floats in water it's less fresh; if it sinks it's fresher.

questions.question: If you ignore somebody or shun somebody, you give them the cold shoulder. Why is it called the cold shoulder?

answers.answer: When the country was split into kingdoms, knights traveling into another kingdom could demand a peasant put them up for the night. The peasant couldn't refuse, but the only way to tell them to leave was to serve them a cold shoulder of meat, signalling it was time to go.

questions.question: Is there a reason why the lights on all emergency vehicles are blue as opposed to red or green?

answers.answer: Blue light was deemed the brightest light, especially at night time for emergency vehicles. The UK only has blue and red on the rear of emergency vehicles when stationary because the red light means danger, allowing drivers to see it's an emergency vehicle and take avertive action. The blue is more visible at night.

questions.question: Why do we get dizzy? Why do we get that nausea feeling when we spin around and what's the chemical thing that makes it happen? Like, ballerinas don't get it, maybe they train themselves out of it. It feels like a hangover.

answers.answer: There's a liquid in your ear canal that acts almost like a spirit level. When you spin, this liquid gets whipped up. Once you stop spinning, there's a conflict in your brain as your eyes are fixed but the liquid in your ear is still moving, giving you the dizzy sensation.

It's not that the liquid continues to spin around in your ear. Your brain processes vestibular information differently for different people and for different periods of time. Some people go on roller coasters and seek it and don't feel dizzy for long. The vestibular system changes as you get older - most people process more of the sensory vestibular information as they age, which is why they like spinning less than children do.

questions.question: Is it illegal to tickle in wrestling? (Her 8-year-old son and husband asked)

answers.answer: Yes. In the 90s there was a character called Doink the Clown who used tickling under the arms as one of his moves to antagonise opponents. He was later paired with his tag team partner Dink the Clown.
Although Doink the Clown did employ tickling as opponent baiting technique during the heyday of WWE, he wasn't actually technically supposed to.

questions.question: Why can't you refreeze food after it's been defrosted? On frozen tuna in a vacuum pack it says 'do not refreeze'. Is that instruction still accurate if it's completely airtight vacuum packed?

answers.answer: When Clarence Birdseye discovered that food tastes horrid after freezing, he found that slow freezing creates large crystals that burst the cells of food and destroy it. Quick freezing between key temperatures produces very small crystals that don't destroy the cell membranes, so food tastes lovely afterwards. The only reason you don't re-freeze after defrosting is because it would taste rank, not because it would kill you.

Vacuum packing isn't like sealing something in a can - bacon is vacuum packed but goes off quickly. Freezing doesn't kill bacteria, it just slows down their rate of reaction. If you take something out of the freezer, bacteria warm up and start metabolising and reproducing. If you put it back in the freezer, you've got heightened levels of bacteria which may infect whoever eventually eats it.

questions.question: How do fireworks display hearts and images and stars when they go off in the sky?
What is the reason for the dark patches on the moon? We know there's no water, no oceans, so what creates the dark patches?

answers.answer: When the Earth was formed, a big planet-shaped object hit it and caused the main gray part of the moon. The moon circulated the Earth collecting debris and turned into the ball we see. The darker bits are impacts from asteroids - craters and topographic features. When a meteorite hits, it displaces the top layer of dust which reflects light differently from other areas.

questions.question: Is Adam related to Jesus? In what way? Who's the daddy?
When did John Wayne pull a pint at The Castle pub in Tooting? There's a picture behind the bar of him actually pulling a pint but nobody knows when he did it.

answers.answer: In the early 70s there was a Tooting carnival and John Wayne was sitting in a car waving at the people. Someone suggested the castle was in Tooting and he might have gone in for a quick pint.

questions.question: Why is water sometimes slippery and other times gives you more grip? Like supermarket wet floor signs saying slippery, but you lick your finger to get more grip on plastic bags or newspaper pages.

topics: zero vs O in phone numbers

questions.question: Why have people started saying zero instead of O when reading out phone numbers?

answers.answer: It's because we're doing more with computers and machines. When working with telegrams at the Post Office, you had to clarify whether you were saying numbers or letters. Now there's more call for clarity. Also, if you typed an O into a password that should be a number, it would get confused.

questions.question: Why when you start a phone number with O are you using a letter rather than a number?
Is there a historical connection between the Irish accent and the Caribbean accent?

answers.answer: A lot of Irish immigrants to America got very bad colds on the ship on the way over, and that is why the American accent is actually an Irishman with a blocked nose.

The Caribbean accents come from the colonial past. The British sent Irish sailors and Irish workers to the Caribbean. Also, the British sent Irish people as slaves to the Caribbean and America. So there would have been Irish influence on the accent.

My dad's from Montserrat, known as the Emerald Isle of the Caribbean. Irish prisoners and slaves were sent to work in the plantations. My surname is Lynch, which is an Irish connection. The accent was taken on by linguistic osmosis - that's where the similarities like 'tree' and 'three' come from.

questions.question: Why does our brain see some people as ugly and some people as attractive?

answers.answer: The answer is sex, ultimately. To procreate, you have to be aroused by what is attractive. If you got aroused by everything, you'd be in all sorts of trouble. It's evolutionary - so we're not all chasing the same person.

It's down to evolutionary psychology. Women have been looking for men who are fit enough to run after food and avoid predators - so they're looking for someone with little fat, powerful shoulders, taller, confident, dominant. Men look for healthy women with wide hips who can bear children. It's all about survival of your genes.

questions.question: How are we supposed to know what the law is, given there are obscure laws introduced nearly every week and ignorance is no defence?

answers.answer: I think it's a process of intellectual osmosis. If a law isn't obscure and is important, everyone will be telling each other about it. You learn some at school, some from parents, some from signs, some from books like the Highway Code. Shopkeepers learn mannequin laws at mannequin training.
Whoever passes the laws has a responsibility to ensure people are aware of them. They put it on the statute book and once it's there, it spreads by intellectual osmosis, dissipation and dilution.

The law of the land is common law jurisdiction - as long as you don't cause harm, injury and loss to anybody, you've not broken any law. Legislation is statutory and requires the consent of the governed.

questions.question: Why in football is the referee known as the referee and in cricket he's known as the umpire?
Why when you get your keys out at your front door does your bladder give up and you suddenly desperately need to pee, even though you could hold it for hours getting home?

answers.caller: Helen from Wadhurst (speech and language therapist)
answers.answer: Your brain is clever. To go to the loo, your brain sends messages to your bladder saying 'you can go now'. Your brain realises you're nearly home, so it starts getting ready. Because your bladder is so full with significant pressure behind it, it's hard to hold that last bit. It's like trying to stop mid-weeing - it's difficult with a full bladder, easier with an empty one. You can't fool your brain into thinking you're not home.

questions.question: How do long-distance train drivers get home after their last train? For example, if they drive from Falmouth to Scotland, how do they get back?

answers.answer: They don't drive all the way from Falmouth to Scotland. They start at their home depot, do a small portion of the route, then drive another train back. They end up where they started - it's about their base.

A train driver signs on at his home depot, books on duty, drives a train, and ends up back at his home depot. They won't drive all the way from Falmouth to Scotland - they only do a small portion of the route and then drive another train back in the opposite direction. It's all about the base.

questions.question: Why are planets and stars spherical while asteroids and comets are not?

answers.answer: Planets over billions of years have been filed down to become circular through being in orbit and hitting things. Asteroids and comets are the bits being knocked off them. (Jonesy said size has something to do with it.)

If a body is big enough, the force of gravity overcomes the strength of the material and pulls it into a spherical shape. For stars, gas doesn't take much force to be pulled round. Dwarf planets like Ceres are just about big enough to pull themselves into a sphere. Smaller asteroids are more elongated because they're too small for gravity to overcome their material strength. It's about size and gravity, not orbit.

questions.question: My baby didn't respond at all to the disgusting smell of dog mess while adults around were retching. At what age do we start associating a smell with something nasty and making it smell bad to us?

answers.answer: The baby can smell the bad smell but has no reference that it's disgusting. It's a learned behaviour. We are conditioned to find things disgusting. There's a documentary called 'The Anatomy of Disgust' about this. Babies don't find poo disgusting - they have to be taught not to try to eat it. Revulsion at dangerous things is learned. Even with smelly cheeses, we balk at the smell even though they taste delicious, because our parents taught us those smells usually mask something unhealthy.

questions.question: Why can't you buy duck or pork stock? In every supermarket I've ever been in, I've never seen pork stock, fresh or in stock cubes, and the same for duck. Why not?

answers.answer: You can buy chicken stock but probably not enough duck meat consumed to have lots of bones left over. Pork stock might not be very nice.
You can get pork stock but you have to go to one of the larger supermarkets.

questions.question: Why are the Downs called the Downs when we're always up high, like Dunstable Downs?

answers.answer: The word 'Downs' comes from the Gaelic word 'Dunn' (D-U-N-N) which means hill or hill fort.

questions.question: The Earth rotates around the Sun and rotates on its own axis, but the Moon does not rotate around its axis, and most moons around planets don't rotate while their planets do. Why? We always see the same side of the moon.

answers.answer: The moon is very slightly egg-shaped, and being egg-shaped, the heaviest side of the moon will always face towards the largest source of gravity, which is the Earth.

The moon does rotate, but it rotates at the same rate as the Earth, so it appears not to rotate. The gravity has produced a bulge, and that bulge is attracted to the Earth, so the moon's bulge effectively keeps it in lock, in synchronism with the Earth's rotation.

questions.question: Why is it that we speak English and use the English alphabet, but when Indian and Chinese people write their names like Mahandring Singh or Kim Jong-un or Tai Chi Chu, it's spelled in English? Why do the Chinese and Indians use the English alphabet to spell their names?

answers.answer: Because you're reading it in English. If you were reading a Korean newspaper, it wouldn't say Kim Jong-un - it would be characters. Indian names are phonetic - the sounds denoted by Sanskrit or Chinese characters are emulated by a collection of letters. Like 'Ranjit' - it's not a six-letter word in Sanskrit but the sounds will be the same, they just reproduce the sounds.

questions.question: Why are the perforations between the squares on toilet paper made so uselessly small? No one ever wants a single sheet - that size of paper is of no use to anyone. Is there some reason they're that size?

If you had a nuclear explosion in space, would it be a big bang like the Hiroshima bomb, or would it just be like a damp banger in a firebox? There's no atmosphere in space, so would you get a big bang or just go poof? Would it still destroy things?
I changed my kitchen lights from halogen to LEDs and my digital radio stopped working. When I turned the LEDs off, the radio started again. LED lights seem to interfere with digital radio - why?

answers.answer: LED lights contain a switch mode power supply that converts 240V AC to DC. Cheap or poor quality ones produce electrical noise/hash that leaks back into the mains wiring of the house. This creates an antenna effect throughout the house wiring. The DAB radio is trying to pick up a weak signal from a transmitter 10 miles away. If the hash level exceeds the received signal level, DAB stops working because it's binary - it's either there or not there. That's why the radio just cuts out rather than getting worse gradually.

questions.question: In a fish and chip shop, why do they only batter the sausage and not the sallower? I would like a battered sallower.

The word 'representative' in 'representative APR' - what does it mean and why is it always in there? If you buy a car on 4% APR, you're going to pay 4% APR. Why do you have to have the word representative in?

How come, when you don't have to get up, you don't want to stay in bed? When you do have to get up, nothing would please you more than the phone ringing and someone saying 'you're fired, you can stay in bed today'?

answers.answer: There are five stages of sleep. Stage one is light snooze, stage five is REM. You start at stage one, go to five, then back to one and wake up. Alarms can wake you in stages two, three, four - when you're in stage four you're groggy and want to go back to sleep to get back to stage one. When you go to bed without an alarm on Saturday, your body knows around what time to wake you up and releases chemicals. So even if you think you can go back to sleep, your body is already preparing you to wake up. It's just the body clock.

questions.question: Is it true that when you shave, the hair grows back thicker?

answers.answer: No, it doesn't. There's no reason the follicle should suddenly decide to grow thicker hair just because someone shaved it. It's dead protein to start with. It's an optical illusion - something shorter appears thicker, and possibly it's slightly thicker at the base as it dries out and tapers toward the tip.

questions.question: How do they determine an animal's sense of smell? When they say dogs have a sense of smell 50 times greater than humans, and sharks can detect a drop of blood from a mile away, how do they know this?

answers.answer: It's down to the number of scent receptors in their nose. Some dogs have more scent receptors than others - these are called tracking dogs, like bloodhounds.

questions.question: What's the point of wasps?

answers.answer: They capture aphids and green flies. They're pollinators - every time they land on a flower and get covered in pollen, then land on another flower, they transfer it. Without wasps and other flying insects, flowers would never breed.
The main purpose of wasps is predation. They do pollinate but it's a by-product - they're not as hairy as bees. Their thorax picks up some pollen but not to the degree bees do.
Research from Brazil confirms wasps act as pollen vectors and have been recorded with pollen grains attached to their exoskeleton, confirming their pollinating habit.

questions.question: Can I dye my ex-girlfriend's white lap dog to look like a tiger to win her back before Valentine's?

answers.answer: You can dye your dog, but you cannot use chemicals you'd use on your own hair. You need vegetable dye-based dyes. You can get them from a grooming supplier's pet grooming site. It's called 'creative grooming' and there are specialists who do this. It's not as simple as just sticking dye on in a few lines - you have to divide it, put cream or conditioner on parts you don't want to dye that particular color, or use a stencil with a compressor.
Almost unanimous opposition - you shouldn't do it.
If somebody dyed my dog like a tiger, I would kill them.

questions.question: What is the newest professional sport?

answers.answer: Video games - e-sports. Kids are now making a living playing video games. If people pay to watch it, it's a sport, like darts or bowls.
Video games is the answer. It's become a universal thing in the States - they're giving scholarships to gamers in sports programs. League of Legends had big tournaments in stadiums.
While e-gaming has been professional for years, Ultimate Frisbee is actually the newest professional sport. It's only about a year or so old that teams are being paid. It's massive in America.

questions.question: Why is being famous called being 'in the limelight'? Why is the light light?

answers.answer: Probably because of calcium carbonate - lime is so bright white that the brightest white light on stage was known as limelight. Being in the limelight meant being in the prominent position on stage, and that got picked up to mean being in a prominent position.

Back in the olden days in theatres, the lighting was done with calcium and lime. If you were in the lime light, you were in the shiniest part of the stage. I learned this when I was 13 - my aunt Diana Dawes was famous and described as being 'in the limelight' in newspapers, so I looked it up at Acton Library.

questions.question: Where does 'scran' come from, what has it got to do with food? In the army we use a term for having food. As well as scoff, you've got scran.

answers.answer: It's Scottish. It's certainly Scottish. I think it's northern, but I don't know why. I don't know why it's a word for food.

questions.question: How do people who are blind know where braille is written? For example, I was in a toilet recently and there was a sign that said 'press here to flush' but it was written in braille underneath. If I was blind, would I have to run my hands over the whole wall trying to find that?

answers.answer: Just habit and familiarity. There's not going to be a specific sort of way of knowing. It's just usually it will be there. If you're at the traffic crossing, then you know to put your hand underneath the button-pressing device to get the special blind person's buzzy thing.

There's approximately 2 million people blind in this country, but only 2% of them can't see anything at all. That's where people get this misconception. Because you can actually, I'm registered blind myself, but I can see certain bits. I wouldn't be rubbing my hand all over a toilet wall to find out. You sort of know roughly where the button is or the handle to flush the toilet. There's a fairly small catchment area where it could be. Even if you're fully blind, the 2% that can't see anything at all, they would know where the flusher is from experience.

questions.question: Where's grass seed come from?

answers.answer: Grass. You mow it. The reason you don't see grass seed is because you cut it. If you don't mow it, seeds come out.

questions.question: What's the distinction between a narrator and a commentator? We were watching TV last night and wanted to find out who the narrator was to come down with us. But my girlfriend said he's a commentator. He comments on what action is taking place.

answers.answer: When it's been written in advance and he reads it out, he's narrating. If it's coming off the top of his head in response to what he can see, it's commentating. It doesn't matter whether it's Big Brother, Come Dine With Me, or the FA Cup. If it's off the top of his head, it's commentating. If it's written down in advance, it's narrating. It's that simple.

questions.question: Did women in the Middle Ages shave their legs?

answers.answer: It dates back to 500 BC. Roman ladies used to rub their legs with plummy stones. But it even goes further back than that. Ancient Egyptians had no body hair at all, because it was deemed as being cleaner. So they pluck it out.

It goes back to the early 1900s, 1920s. When women started exposing their legs. Skirts started getting shorter. And a certain razor company in America saw a market. And they started advertising for women to shave their legs and under their arms.

questions.question: What would be the boundaries of a local beef? I was watching a Marco Pierre White advert where he asks if the beef is locally sourced and the butcher says yes, 70 miles away. I don't class 70 miles as being local.

answers.answer: It might not mean anything. It might just mean Britain. In comparison to Argentina, yes, of course it's local. But as a lorry driver, I don't consider 70-mile drives to get some beef as being local.
Locally sourced is defined by Europe. It defines a geographical area where it comes from. But it could be as big as America or Russia. Or it could be as big as Wensley.

questions.question: What is the shelf life of an unopened bottle of tequila? In 1986 I bought a bottle of tequila and I haven't touched it since then.

answers.answer: It'll be fine. I would have thought strong stuff. What's the worst that can happen as long as it's sealed? A spirit? I don't know. It might mature in the bottle. It might do.

It's a rectified spirit, so no, it shouldn't go off, because if you think of things like whiskey and brandy, which sit in the barrel for many years open to the air, the only thing that happens is that they evaporate slightly. But rectified spirits are used to preserve medical specimens. So, yeah, it wouldn't go off. And especially as it's been sealed down, it won't evaporate either. 1986, still going strong. Should be the same strength. All he needs is a bit of salt and a few lemons or limes.

Those long bits of grass towards the periphery of any sort of lawn tend to have little bits like corn growing out the top of them. We used to call them flea darts. We used to chuck them at each other and get them stuck on our school jumpers. That's how we found out where grass seed was.

questions.question: How does snowplough drivers get to work?

answers.answer: They either go to work on a snowplough or they walk. It's not exactly rocket science.

Weather forecasting now is so accurate from the Met Office that we know when the snow is coming. So snowplough drivers are already at work before the snow. They drive or walk there. Sometimes they go the night before, but other times they walk.

questions.question: Why does it, when you drink alcohol at lunchtime, it seems to make you feel more tired than when you do in the evening?

answers.answer: When you drink at lunchtime, you then have to go and do other stuff - school run, go back to the office. If you drink in the evening, you're not really doing anything else. You're just having fun, having a nice time.

questions.question: I was on a plane last night coming back from China, and exactly in line with the windows of the aircraft was the moon. You had to actually look slightly down at it. So how come when the moon's 230,000 miles away, up above the earth, when you're flying at seven miles above the earth, do you actually look down on the moon?

answers.answer: Draw a big circle for the earth. Put a tiny dot at one o'clock for the plane. Then go to 11 o'clock and go about ten times further out from the original circle and draw another circle for the moon. Now draw a line between the dot and the second circle. The line just skims the earth. The line is straight. The moon is at the same level as the plane, even though it's much, much further away from the earth than the plane.

questions.question: How are we able to work out what's in the middle of the Earth? Is there anywhere below where has actually been successfully drilled? I just believe that we know nothing of the things that we speak of in some instances.
Can GPs self-prescribe, or must they see another GP to get prescriptions?

answers.answer: I think it's memory. When you're a baby, you're happy every morning you get up. Whatever they say you're going to do, you go off with a happy face. As you get older, you learn that some things are not nice or a bore or onerous. So, for example, first time you go to a dentist, you're happy. He drills, causes pain. Next time someone says Monday you're going to the dentist, you're unhappy.

questions.question: Why when you don't have to get up can you not go back to sleep, but when you do have to get up you can't think of anything you'd rather do than stay in bed and go back to sleep?
What's scran?
Why is space dark? Why doesn't the whole space light up from the sun like it does on Earth during daytime?

answers.answer: Light is invisible, and if there's nothing for it to reflect off, you can't actually see it. So, once it's travelling through space, you can't see it. As soon as you put an object in the way of the light, it reflects, and then that's what you see. You don't actually see the light. You see what's reflected off of.

Any point light, the energy and the light will dissipate in a cube relationship the further you get away from it. Space is dark because there's far too much distance between all the stars, and that was one of the pieces of evidence that was put forward for the fact that our universe is expanding. The nearest star (beyond our sun) is approximately 4.2 light years away.

questions.question: What causes the wind to blow from a particular direction? Why does it blow from the north or the south? Why do we get a west wind? Why doesn't all wind go in the same direction? From one morning to the next, it can go in all points of the compass.

answers.answer: It boils down to the Coriolis effect. The sun heats the equator quicker than the poles. The equator rises, draws in cold air from the poles, and the northern hemisphere goes one way, the southern hemisphere the other. You also have high and low pressures. High pressure, the wind goes anti-clockwise. Low pressure goes clockwise. Depending where you are in relation to these pressures determines wind direction.

questions.question: Why is a foot a foot? Twelve inches is one foot. The foot was somebody's actual foot. Twelve inches is a men's size 16 shoe. My son-in-law takes size 16 shoes and I measured his foot - it's exactly 12 inches. So whose foot, when they standardized the measurements, was actually a size 16?

answers.answer: St Paul's Cathedral was the origin of the foot measurement. Churches and cathedrals had marketplaces outside, and a post there became a standard size for selling wood and cloth.
The foot goes right back to ancient Rome and ancient Greece. The measurement was called a pous in Greek. It has nothing to do with St Paul's.

questions.question: Why do we wear a wedding ring on that particular finger? Why not any other of the fingers?

answers.answer: There's a vein in your ring finger that goes all the way to your heart. It's not in the other five fingers.
Hand on heart - the answer is related to the heart metaphor.
You were wrong about the wedding ring answer. I Googled it.

questions.question: How do you become a private detective?
Why do places like Clapham have North, South, Common, but no West? Why does Croydon have East, South, and West Croydon but no North Croydon? Why don't they use all four points of the compass?

answers.answer: It's about stations. Places only get compass names if a station is built there. West Croydon has a station, East Croydon has a station, but there's no North Croydon station.

questions.question: What happens to hotel mini soaps? Do they throw them away after two or three uses? Do they get recycled?

answers.answer: A very small amount is used in staff areas and public cloakrooms. The rest is thrown away. Years ago there was a market for reselling it to be melted down and reshaped, but now production costs are so low it's cheaper to throw it all away. I was a purchasing manager for a group of hotels.

questions.question: Why is it hot in the Caribbean and cold in Europe or America? Why are some countries hotter than others?

answers.answer: The earth is round, so different points on the planet are different distances from the sun. The closer you are to the equator, the closer you are to the sun. This relates to axial inclination - the earth is tilted.

questions.question: Why when you have a horrible cold or awful flu do you feel so much worse in the evening and at night compared to the day?

answers.answer: I suspect it's because you're not on the go. You stop. Your body prepares for sleep. No distractions. Things function more slowly.
You just notice it more because you haven't got the distraction.

questions.question: Why on the day you don't have to go to work do you want to get up early instead of having a lie-in?

answers.answer: Subconsciously you don't want to waste the day. On days you have to go to work you want to stay in bed, but on days off you're up and about because you know you can be more productive. You want to make the most of the day.

questions.question: Why is it that the majority of food tastes better hot than cold?

answers.answer: Molecular agitation. Heat means you've got more flavour washing around your mouth and taste buds and palate than you would have if it's cold.

Flavour is a combination of smell and taste in a ratio of about 30% taste, 70% smell. Hot food causes more volatiles to evaporate and diffuse faster. The nose is more important than the mouth - when you have a cold and say you can't taste anything, you actually can't smell anything.

questions.question: Do mammals crossing railway tracks that touch the live wire get electrocuted? We know birds don't because they're not earthed, but what about badgers with short legs touching the live wire and grounding?

answers.answer: I'm pretty sure they'd die, but I'm not certain. Animals learn from pain though - they don't do dangerous things again.

There is no Earth on the live rails. When you touch both the live and return rail together, you complete the circuit. Animals would need to touch both at the same time to fry - like a very long badger stretching across. Workers on the Underground could sit on live rails eating sandwiches because they weren't touching the ground.

The underground is DC, not AC. The outside rail is at positive potential, the middle rail is the return at negative potential. If you sit on the line with your feet on the ground, you earth electricity and you die. If you jump up and stand with both feet on the line, you're fine. One foot on ground, one on line = fry. Birds and animals can jump on the line but if they then touch the ground, they die.

questions.question: Why is a building called a building when it's already been built? Why isn't it called a built?

answers.answer: Building can be both a verb and a noun - it's a homonym. You can say 'I am building' (verb) and 'here is a building' (noun). The same applies to words like housing, casing, etc.

questions.question: After many years of driving all over the place, I see lorries with horses written on them. Is this a legal requirement? If it is, why don't cars have people written on them?

answers.answer: There's no legal requirement. It's purely courtesy information. Horse box drivers will slow down for traffic issues because of the danger of horses rattling around. Other animals are usually transported in crates or pens where they don't need to worry about sudden stops. Horses are valuable - if a cow breaks a leg on the way to slaughter, who cares? But horses are going to shows or stables.
Because 'elephant' would be entirely inaccurate.

questions.question: My 8-year-old daughter had pins and needles and asked 'Mummy, why is it called pins and needles?'

answers.answer: It's called pins and needles because the physical sensation feels just like being pricked with pins and needles. They named the condition after what it feels like.

questions.question: Why can't you use laughing gas on the battlefield? Why not carpet bomb somewhere like Aleppo with laughing gas, then go in with gas masks and capture fighters asleep or laughing?

answers.answer: The greatest military minds of the last 200 years haven't thought of it yet. They'd be doing it if it worked.

Chemical weapons need to be heavier than air to sink down and affect people - otherwise they'd float away. The French tried hydrogen cyanide (lighter than air) in WWI and found the lethal radius was less than if they'd just used explosives. Nitrous oxide also wears off very quickly. If it would work, they'd be doing it.

questions.question: What is 'muscle memory' when my golf pro tells me to develop it?

answers.answer: Muscle memory is about coordination stored in your brain. When you address the ball in exactly the same way as when you hit it perfectly, there's a recognition factor in your consciousness. The muscle memory is when you've got everything just right - the pro keeps telling you to develop it because you can't repeat the perfect shot if you've forgotten how it felt.

questions.question: Is there actually any difference between shower gel and shampoo? Does the same thing work for both?

answers.answer: Professor Howell explained that in his household they use one container for everything. Shampoo, soap, and all the rest are the same stuff. The ingredients are the same - it's all marketing, branding and advertising. The expensive ones add perfume and fancy things like tiny pearls, but otherwise it's identical.

questions.question: Why when you boil water twice and make a cup of tea with it does it taste completely different? It gets a furry taste.

answers.answer: You deoxygenate the water when you boil it. Water has air in it, and the boiling process releases the air. The more you boil it, the more air you remove. Frozen boiled water is clear while frozen non-boiled water is cloudy because the air has been taken out. There's also something about hard and soft water affecting tea quality.

questions.question: Why do people go brrrr in the cold?

answers.answer: Friction. When you rub your hands together, friction turns kinetic energy into heat energy. When you go brrrr with your mouth, exactly the same thing is happening - friction converts kinetic energy into heat energy, warming your lips.

questions.question: Why is it that when you don't have to get up at half past six in the morning, you really don't want to stay in bed, but when you do have to get up at half past six, you absolutely want to stay there?
What exactly is a D-notice? How do you know they exist if you're running a newspaper?

answers.answer: I don't know how you find out they exist if you're running a small newspaper. I think Special Branch would come and tell you. But even if I did know, I wouldn't be allowed to tell you anyway.

questions.question: Why is New York also known as the Big Apple?

answers.answer: It was a big, big advertising campaign in the 1970s by the sort of New York tourist authority. Then there's been research into it to find out whether the advertising bloke invented it. A sports writer in the 1920s used to describe it as the Big Apple. And if you go right back to source, there was a line in an economic book that said something about the Big Apple getting more of the nutrients from the tree or something like that when writing about New York status in American. And I think that's pre-1920s.

questions.question: Why does a thumbs up mean everything's good?

answers.answer: It started with Roman emperors. When the Gladiator's got the sword over his enemy and they look at the emperor and if he puts his thumb up, the guy lives. And if he puts his thumb down, the guy dies. That's the earliest example I can think of. So that would translate into good news, I'm allowed to live.

It's at the Colosseum, but it's actually a myth that thumbs-up meant you got to live and thumbs-down meant you were to die. It was actually the opposite. If the emperor kept his thumb up, you had to stay and continue to fight or be eaten by a lion. If he put his thumb down, it meant you got to go back to the gallows and live another day. But because we naturally associate up with being benign and heavenly, over time it's become inverted.

questions.question: Does putting your hand to your forehead, squinting your eyes, and pulling a stupid face make you see any further?

answers.answer: The tunnel effect you create probably does provide a greater degree of focus, but you want to hear it from an eye expert.

answers.caller: Professor Martin Smith (Middlesex University - Professor of Robotics)
answers.answer: Yes, it does work. If you make the size of the hole you look through smaller and smaller, you improve the focus. Because the light coming in... you're capturing a narrower and narrower pencil beam of light and that enables you to focus on closer objects. That applies to both squinting and shielding your eyes. When you shield your eyes, you reduce the field of vision. Only if you reduce the diameter of the sort of cone of light. So squinting definitely works. With regard to shielding your eyes with your hand on your forehead, that would have more to do with shading it from light that would be blinding or overload the sensory system.

questions.question: Is Cleopatra's Needle the oldest thing in London? Is it older than London?
Is the speed of 88 miles an hour in Back to the Future scientifically significant to the ability to travel in time?

answers.answer: Probably because it looked nicest on the old-fashioned digital printer. Every single bit of it would have been lit up. I don't think there's any scientific significance to the fact that Doc Brown's DeLorean was travelling at 88 miles an hour when the flux capacitor kicked in.
If you take an eight and you flip it sideways, it becomes the infinity sign. And that's why it's used in time travel.

671 miles per second is the only recognised speed for potential time travel according to Einstein's theory on time travel - unless you're travelling at the speed of light or faster, it can't happen. That's the real answer. However, in the movies, 88 miles an hour isn't actually relevant because there's a scene where Doc isn't travelling at any speed when time traveling - the lightning strikes him and he goes back to the West.

questions.question: Why did the Vikings have a cross painted on their shields if they were pagans? Does the cross symbol predate Christianity?

answers.answer: The cross on the Viking shields was one of two things depending on when it was. One was they would use the cross to link their other symbols together - if they had a line on the top and an axe on the bottom, it would combine them all together making it look like a four-way insignia rather than random stickers. So it's a geometric decision rather than a religious one. The other one, from a long time ago, is the cross represents the four corners of the earth, which is to protect them from spells from the god. I think it's Mesopotamian or something like that.

questions.question: If you light a fire you need oxygen to burn. In space there's nothing, no oxygen. How does the sun burn?

answers.answer: It's not a fire, mate. It's a massive nuclear explosion. It's nuclear fusion. It does not need oxygen to burn. Unlike a fire which needs oxygen.

answers.caller: Professor Hal (University of Brighton - Professor of the Public Understanding of Science)
answers.answer: The original caller was quite correct. Normally when you have a chemical combustion, you need a fuel, an oxidant, and heat - that's all to do with electrons orbiting the nucleus being transferred. A star is a completely different proposition. It's a nuclear fusion reaction where deuterium and tritium are squashed together to form helium. You don't need oxygen. It's all to do with nuclei and not to do with electrons orbiting. Chemical reactions are to do with electrons which orbit atoms, nuclear reactions are to do with nuclei which are in the center of atoms. They're completely different - chalk and cheese.

questions.question: Why do slugs and snails on the land die if you put salt on them, when there are sea slugs that live surrounded by salt?

answers.answer: The sea slug is a different species - you might as well say how come fish can breathe underwater and humans can't. [The word 'osmosis' was mentioned by caller and then explored]. Salt sucks all the fluid out of the slug and the slug dies. It creates a chemical process.

questions.question: Why do wind farms and wind turbines have to be turned off when it gets too windy?

answers.answer: In case they defeat the objects. It would be a bit like being in a go-kart going down a hill. You want to go fast, but why have you got brakes? Because there comes a point where you will have built up so much speed that the go-kart rattles to pieces, falls apart and crashes. The same with a wind turbine - it spins and spins but can reach a speed at which the spinning is not safe. So it's better to turn it off. Anything can break up if the velocity is too high. The friction will create kinetic energy which contributes to the actual dismantling of the apparatus.

questions.question: How did they know the world was round when the whole world thought it was flat? Atlas is carrying a round earth and he's definitely before Christ.

answers.answer: The Greeks knew about the roundness of the earth from the horizon. When people believed the earth was flat, they couldn't account for the fact that a ship would hove into view over the horizon, which proves there's a current curvature to the surface of the earth. Pythagoras was an ancient Greek doing his work as a geometrist in the years before the birth of Christ. Aristotle, Pythagoras, Socrates, Euclid - they just worked it out. The reason they call it the Dark Ages is because a lot of the knowledge that had been accrued by humanity prior to the Dark Ages just got lost for a while after the Romans left Britain.

questions.question: How does the smell of cooking transfer to every single room within the property when no windows are open, no doors are open, and I'm not walking around fast?

answers.answer: Convection is the word. Heat circulates. Heat rises. Just imagine you open an oven, what happens? You get a blast of that hot air in your face. And it's consistently hot because as you're cooking, things are getting hotter and hotter. That's convection - same way radiators work, same way you heat up a room from a single radiator.
I would agree with Ian but add that it's Brownian motion - when the molecules shake around and that's what makes it spread.
The more heating you've got on, the hotter the house, the more the smells will permeate up the stairs.

questions.question: What does it mean when town signs say 'Welcome to Seven Oaks' and underneath it says 'Twinned with so and so'?

answers.answer: It's towns being pen pals. It allows councilors to travel on fact-finding missions, get freebies and jollies on council expenses. Town twinning allows elected councillors to arrange exchanges for students, visit the twinned town on council expenses, compare cultural artefacts and deepen relationships. It's just like being a town and having a pen pal, but also being able to go and visit the pen pal on council expenses.

Cleopatra's Needle is not the oldest man-made structure in London. There is the Olduvai stone chopping tool from the Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania, currently resident in the British Museum, estimated to be between 1.8 and 2 million years old. It's about 1,500 years BC at best, which is peanuts compared to that.

questions.question: What is the difference between a preserve and a conserve?
Are cats the only animals in the world that purr?

answers.answer: Humans show signs of happiness. Dogs wag their tail.

questions.question: When a bird is on an overhead wire, why does it not become electrocuted like we would?

answers.answer: It's not earthed. The electrical current has to have a destination. If it's not earthed, it won't pass through because it's got nowhere to go.

questions.question: If there was no gravity, would there be air? Is it the gravity that holds air down, or the atmosphere that pushes it?

questions.answer: Conserve is when you cook the fruit to dispel bacteria and then seal it naturally without adding anything. Preserve is the method of sealing to keep air out. Jam has pectin, sugar, glucose and other additives to give it longer life.

questions.question: In the theatre, why are the downstairs seats called the stalls?

questions.answer: The Earth's atmosphere is held onto the Earth by the Earth's gravitational field. If the gravity wasn't there, we would lose our atmosphere, like smaller bodies in the solar system. The Moon has much smaller gravitational pull and doesn't have much atmosphere.

Phil was right. Water has mass and is held down by gravity, so steam should be too. Air, cooled down enough, will turn into liquid - if you had liquid oxygen in a test tube you could see it had mass and was pulled down. Just because it's a gas doesn't mean mass has disappeared.

questions.question: Does eating cheese before you go to bed really give you nightmares?
Do ladybirds hibernate? Found about 100 of them in his window this morning.
Why do leg hairs stop growing when head hair doesn't? They must grow as you get older but mine haven't got longer.

answers.answer: They don't stop growing. They fall out and grow again all the time. It's a constant cycle of leg hair growth.

questions.question: Why is the word 'tea' used in golf for what you put the ball on and the hole you hit from?

questions.answer: Guinea pigs can purr. If you scratch them down their back or give them their favourite food, they purr. It's quite similar to a cat's purr.

Ladybirds do hibernate, or rather overwinter. The species the gentleman found were probably harlequin ladybirds. They tend to cluster together, unlike our indigenous ladybirds which are more solitary. Harlequin ladybirds came from Japan, were deliberately introduced into the USA to control aphids but it didn't work very well.

questions.question: Why do we have two sets of teeth - first a child's then adult's? Why can't we just have one continuous set of teeth that grows with us? And why can't we grow more after losing them?

answers.answer: Evolution - humans developed the ability to survive to grow a second set of teeth. The ones that developed it lived, the ones that didn't eventually died over thousands of years. As for why we don't grow more - we just don't. It's like asking why you don't grow another leg when you get one chopped off.

questions.question: What does 'piping hot' mean? What is the 'piping' bit and how do I judge if my microwave meal is piping hot?
Can a human survive an entire life just on breast milk or formula milk?

answers.answer: Yes, it would be biologically possible. A 22-year-old could survive on it just like a two-month-old - it's just a question of quantity. You'd need formula rather than actual breast milk though.

questions.answer: Cheese is full of tryptophan and tyrosine - precursors to neurotransmitters. Tryptophan affects serotonin and helps you fall asleep, but tyrosine floods the brain with noradrenaline, the alertness neurotransmitter. So you fall asleep easily but then your brain becomes very active, causing vivid dreams and nightmares. This is why people on MAOIs can't eat cheese.
The original theatres didn't have seats where the stalls now are - they were standing places. The definition of a stall is a standing place, like you still see at the Globe Theatre.

questions.question: Why does time go quicker the older you get?

answers.answer: Time seems to flow past you proportionally to your age. A 10-year-old perceives 5 years differently than a 30-year-old. When you're 40 to 50, it seems to take about half the time as it does for somebody who is 20. It's about becoming complacent and used to life.

Our perception of anything is to do with what we've already learned. To a 10-year-old child, one year is 10% of their whole life - a major significant proportion. To a 50-year-old, one year is 2% of their whole life. And therefore the perception is it feels like a lot less. That's all there is to it.

questions.question: Why do we call the end of a cigarette a dog end?

answers.answer: You sling the dog out in the back garden. Same as fag ends in the olden days. When you see the dog out, you see the fags out. That's what you do.

Shouldn't be dog ends, it should be dock ends. D-O-C-K. It comes from many years ago when dogs had their tails docked, making them a very short stump at the back end. When worker men were smoking and needed to get back to work quickly, their mate would say 'never mind about your fag, just dock it like a dog's.' It's evolved into a dog.

questions.question: Why do all my 65 Christmas cards have different designs? Why don't people choose the same card?

answers.answer: It's not a real mystery. The reason there are so many different Christmas card designs is to avoid precisely what you've described - uniformity. The card industry deliberately produces a dizzying array of designs.

questions.question: Why has the Queen's silhouette on stamps never been updated while the Royal Mint updates the Queen's portrait on coins every ten years or so?
Why can you hear a plane flying overhead loudly from the ground (loud enough to stop a conversation) when if you're on the plane you can hear yourself think?

answers.answer: Two effects: one is down to the genius of sound insulation engineers that the sound isn't transmitted into the aeroplane. The other is that you have a ground effect - when you're by the ground you get all the reflections from the ground and from the buildings around you, which adds to the noise. The main thing is you're in a cylindrical tube and the sound gets reflected around you so the waves go in a different direction. On the ground, every wave coming out of the engine reaches you eventually, and ones that don't reach you directly bounce off other things and reach you that way.

questions.question: Why are there Welsh teams in the English Football League and English teams in the Welsh FA Cup?

answers.answer: Just to make the competition bigger and better. Otherwise you would end up with a similar situation to Scotland where Celtic and Rangers historically win everything - it would be Swansea and Cardiff. The sense of division between Wales and England is not as profound and historical as the sense of division between Scotland and England.

questions.question: Why do ladies' shirts zip and button on the opposite side to men's shirts?

answers.answer: The answer dates back to the days when ladies would have been dressed by their maids. The massive majority of people are right-handed, so if your lady's maid was doing up your blouse, you'd want the buttons on the other side to accommodate her right-handedness. It made it easier for the maid to dress the lady.

questions.question: Why do we eat turkey for Christmas dinner? When did that start and why don't we eat something like a hog roast?
Why is the hard shoulder on the motorway called the 'hard shoulder'?

answers.answer: Soft shoulders were gravel covered while hard shoulders were tarmac covered. The shoulder part comes from when you used to have a ditch running alongside the road. The road centre used to be known as the crown, and you had the shoulder running down to the ditch, known as the arms. A hard shoulder is a filled-in ditch covered in tarmac.

questions.question: Why do people cheer 'hooray' when a barman drops a glass in a pub? When did that tradition start?
Why do I have a high pain threshold? Is it mental/bravery or physical?

answers.answer: We have a central nervous system that controls processes inflammation through our brain. It comes into our muscles, joints, skin, sense of smell, taste. Some people's brain processes more of these sensations more quickly, some process less. Like some people are really bothered by mild sounds or mild smells, and others don't even pick them up. Adrenaline is also a pain reliever in itself. Hormone levels and changes in our body as we grow up changed the way our brain processes information. And also your sensory processing is different in different people.

questions.question: Why do chickens lay different sized eggs?

answers.answer: They can lay different sizes, but most of the time it's the same birds laying the same eggs. If they're a bit under the weather or had a freak-out with thunder or fireworks, they can sometimes lay really tiny ones. The biggest one she ever laid was probably about twice the size of normal ones.

questions.question: Why is the cold tap always on the right-hand side of the sink and hot on the left? Who decided that and why did it catch on?
Why don't babies yawn when adults do? My 10-month-old Jacob doesn't seem to yawn when I yawn, even when he keeps me up at night.

answers.answer: Because Jacob is completely reliant upon you for his security at the moment. So you yawn, it doesn't mean he's safe. He's not going to yawn himself. But he knows you're safe because you've provided him with... You're only safe in terms of what you can see. He doesn't know what you can't see. If he's an adult and he's looking at you, he can see behind you and he knows that you're both safe so you're going to have a cheeky yawn. Yawns are contagious because it speaks of a tribal security that a baby can't be part of because a baby doesn't protect itself.

questions.question: Why are TV and film credits always in Roman Numerals? I always look for the year but have wondered why it's never written as 1943 or whatever year the programme was made.

answers.answer: It's basically because when programmes were first coming around, there were less of them, and if you put the dates in Roman numerals, it made repeats more easy to do, because they were less recognisable as repeats. If you put the dates in normal years, people would realise that it was a programme from five years ago, whereas if you did it in Roman numerals, it would take less people to recognise that. So it was a deliberate tactic designed to camouflage the fact that everything was a repeat.

questions.question: Like taste buds differentiate between different tastes - salty, sweet etc. Can skin cells with nerve cells differentiate between hot and cold, or is it your brain that translates that information? If you jump into a hot shower, it's not instant - the information has to reach your brain via your nervous system. Are there different nerve cells for heat and different ones for cold?

answers.answer: It speaks of a tribal security that a baby can't be part of because a baby doesn't protect itself.

We do have separate sensors for heat and cold. We also have separate sensors for touch and for pain as well. So we've got lots of separate different sensors that do lots of different jobs in the skin, which send messages to the brain.

questions.question: If you blow in a dog's face they get angry with you, but if you take the dog out for a ride, why do they always want to stick their head out the window?

answers.answer: The reason dogs don't like having their face blown in is the same reason you don't, and the reason they like sticking their head out the window is the same reason we like being out in a bracing breeze. If you're on the top of a hill and there's a lovely wind blowing over you, it doesn't irritate you in the way that you'd be irritated if I came up to you now and blew in your face for a short period of time. You're comparing apples with pears. You're not comparing like with like.

questions.question: Have you ever weighed yourself before going to bed and then weighed yourself in the morning and realised you lost weight overnight - sometimes as much as a few pounds? How can you lose that much when nothing's entering or leaving your body?

answers.answer: Think of food as fuel and yourself as an engine. When you're asleep, the engine is idling. It's not actually off. So you're still burning fuel. You're still burning the food that you've taken on during the day. Some of it will be heat energy and some will involve sweating as well. You're probably going to lose more weight overnight when you're hot than when you're cold. As you digest food, as you burn down your fuel, you will also be emitting exhaust gases. So the only reason you would lose weight overnight is because you are burning fuel while you sleep and turning it into heat energy, kinetic energy (you still move when you're asleep), and emitting gases.

questions.question: Are background artists/extras actually talking or just moving their mouths like they're talking? When I see them chatting away in scenes, I'm just not sure if they're actually talking. I was an extra once but can't remember if we were allowed to talk.

answers.answer: They do talk normally. The actors, the sound man will be holding an enormous microphone over the heads of the people talking, and he won't be holding anything over the heads of the people not talking. So the ones who are not talking would be obvious if they were miming. Generally speaking, they're not close enough to have their noise picked up. They often want background noise too.

answers.caller: Alex in Forest Hill (special effects professional)
answers.answer: They don't speak at all. It can alter the signal that they primarily want from the main actors, so they definitely don't. If you're on set and you're watching it, it is absolutely amazing how good they are at it. It looks like they could be talking, but they make it up on the spot. Most recently, on the Christian Bale film Exodus, Captain America, Mr. Selfridge - they never want extras speaking.

questions.question: Does scratching coins on vending machines actually help if they don't work the first time? I've never tried it but I've always seen people do it, and also licking them or applying saliva.

answers.caller: Steve in Southend (former vending engineer for 13 years)
answers.answer: It does help. The way a coin works is that there are two sensors. You drop the coin, it goes past the first sensor, then the second sensor, and the computer works out the time difference between the two sensors. If the coin is dirty or greasy, it slows the coin down and it goes down the chute. You wash the coin or wet the coin, and it speeds the coin up again. Scratching itself shouldn't make any difference - people are probably rubbing or buffing it, removing the grease. So cleaning it would improve its likelihood of working.

questions.question: Why don't snakes attack each other? Most animals of the same species will turn on each other, but I've never seen it with snakes. You see a snake pit and they just wriggle around inside, never see one turn on the other.

answers.answer: Most animals don't fight each other, do they, really? Creatures fight over mates and food. But you might be onto something.

Some snakes do attack each other. The red-bellied black snake will kill the brown snake. The brown snake is actually more dangerous than the red-bellied black snake, so the red-bellied black snake will attack a brown snake.

The cobras eat other snakes. The king cobra is cannibalistic - it eats other cobras and other snakes. And the king snakes, they're cannibalistic too, they eat other snakes. And they do fight for mates as well. When you watch the Indian snake charming and the snake rears up, all snakes can do that and they do that when they're fighting. They twist around each other and they'll fight for a mate.

questions.question: How do living statues who spray themselves and stand still do it? There's a brilliant piece in the Mail today about them. Some of them are elevated. How do they do that? What about the ones with walking sticks?
