They have more dominant birds in the flock who are usually at the front leading, and they swap over when they get tired because flying at the front causes this deflection of air. But they only swap over between the more dominant birds.

questions.question: Why do the signs for service stations on the motorway have a spoon and a fork and not a knife and fork?
Why are we told there are nasty bacteria living in our mouths, yet when we brush our teeth we just put the toothbrush in a cup and leave it overnight? Why aren't we told to sterilize the toothbrush?

answers.answer: The question is almost self-answered. It is advisable to sterilize your toothbrush, but we don't do it because we never have. There will be bacteria gathering on your toothbrush while it's in the cup. It's probably a bad thing, but how big is the risk? Is it worth changing your habits for?

questions.question: What is the role of the policeman that stands outside Number 10 Downing Street? The door never seems to open from the outside, so what is he actually doing there?

answers.answer: Number 10's door can't be opened from outside - it must be opened from inside only. When the officer sees someone he knows approaching, he signals inside for them to open the door. If he doesn't know them, he can send a message for them to open it. He's like a human intercom. He also deters random people from knocking on the door.

To supplement: when James went to Downing Street last week, the charming officer who posed for photos was in full body armour and holding a very large machine gun. That officer is the last line of security.

questions.question: What does 'Bob's your uncle' refer to?

answers.answer: I'll go with Robert Peel, but not with enough confidence to award myself a round of applause.

It refers to Robert Salisbury, from the 1800s. He was prime minister (Robert Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury) who appointed his nephew Arthur Balfour to political positions. The perception was that Balfour only managed to become prime minister because of his uncle's influence, so it became 'Bob's your uncle' meaning something achieved through familial influence.

questions.question: Do Chinese people in China eat English food?

answers.answer: Yes, they do. She had a Chinese exchange student staying with them who said they go out to English restaurants in China as a culinary adventure. The student used knives and forks because she couldn't manage chopsticks with English food like sausage and mash.

questions.question: Why is the UK called the 'Motherland' while other countries like Russia, France and Germany are called the 'Fatherland'? Who decides this?

answers.answer: It's historical. During Britain's biggest period of expansion (imperialism), we had Queen Victoria (a woman) on the throne - she was Empress of the World. The rest of the world referred back to the 'mother' and 'motherland.' The Russians would have the Tsar and Germany would have a Kaiser, hence 'fatherland.' It would be based on the gender of the monarch at the time of most expansion. Russia may also be called 'motherland' because of Catherine the Great.

questions.question: If two people travel in different directions on the M25, both staying on the inside lane, what would be the difference in distance covered?

answers.answer: It's 130 miles going one way and 120 going the other on the inside lane, and he knows because he's driven both ways in the inside lane.

The 10-mile difference theory is wrong. There's hardly any point on the M25 where you cannot see the other carriageway, so the lanes wouldn't need to be quite a way apart all the way around for that to be true. The difference would be a matter of a few metres.

questions.question: What does 'Hale' mean in Tottenham Hale?
Why do macaroons have rice paper attached to the bottom? Why are they cooked with the rice paper on them?

answers.answer: The consistency of the coconut mix is such that whatever you put it on, whether it be metal, plastic, greaseproof paper or whatever, it will stick. The reason they put rice paper on it is so that you can eat the macaroon and the paper is stuck too. It's a baking aid to facilitate removal of macaroon from baking track.

questions.question: Who decided which way around the world should be up or down? When you look at the map, Scotland is above England. What would happen if it was the other way around? The universe has no top or bottom, so who decided north should be at the top?

answers.answer: The top of the planet is decided by the flow of the magnetic field from north to south. You have two poles at each end and the flow from north to south determines the north pole as being the top.

It's complex and paradoxical. They've measured it and split into four levels. The way the Earth is spinning around the sun, the sun seems to rise in the east. When the sun culminates in the midheaven at the highest point, it is known as north because that is the highest point. Also because of the equator, those in the southern hemisphere when the sun culminates for them, it's north for them too. In ancient Egypt, what they called northern Egypt was actually south.

It was down to the invention of the compass and the egocentricity of Europeans. Europeans invented the compass and charted a lot of the world, using the magnetic north when making maps. If you were making a map, you'd put yourself at the centre or top. Most recent maps were made by Europeans, so we put ourselves at the top. It's an imperial legacy. The Europeans invented the printing press which distributed those maps, and while other cultures may have had different maps with south at north, their maps didn't survive or get distributed. It's simply tradition built upon imperial or technological superiority.

questions.question: My dog sleeps on my bed and every night he circles in the same spot several times, going round and round as though chasing his tail. Why does he do this?

answers.answer: It's evolution. In the savannahs of old, he'd have been making his bed in long grass. He's padding down the grass so that he can have a nice sleep without any stray blades going up his nostrils.

questions.question: The county badge of Essex is three scimitar swords. Scimitar swords are Middle Eastern origin. Why three scimitar swords?

answers.answer: They're not actually scimitars or cutlasses - they're saxes or seaxes, a type of weapon favored by the Saxons. If you weren't high rank, you nearly always carried a sax, which was like a cross between a big knife and a sword - a single-edged weapon like a very big bowie knife with a clipped edge at the top. As it's been stylised in heraldry, it's turned into what looks like a scimitar. This is a reference to Essex's historical past. Essex is the kingdom of the East Saxons (just as Sussex is the kingdom of the South Saxons and Wessex is the kingdom of the West Saxons).

questions.question: Why do all the continents begin and end with the same letter? Europe, America, Australia, Asia, Africa, Antarctica

answers.answer: The Romans. Europe would originally in Latin times have been Europa. So the question becomes why do all the continents end in A? The answer is the Romans - they were named at a time when most things were in Latin for official language.

questions.question: Is there a benchmark by which developing countries and emerging economies become developed? When does a country cease to be developing and become developed?
I work on buildings and sometimes see plants growing from the top of roofs - just poking out the grouting with no soil. How do they actually grow there?

answers.answer: Plants don't need soil - they just need water and light. They'll get their nutrients from rainwater and dust.

A lot of it is because pigeons eat stuff off grass and do their business on roofs and gutters. Some types of stuff also get into building materials. Weeds can grow no matter what you do. All they need is light and water - they don't actually need soil.

questions.question: I've just painted my front room white (from dark brown and light brown). Now the room is echoey. Everything is back in - furniture, carpet - just the paint color is different. Why would painting it white make the room more echoey?

answers.answer: White paint has reflective properties in it, which is why you get an echo. It reflects sound. Darker paint absorbs sound.
It's the wallpaper that makes the difference. When you take wallpaper off a wall, sound bounces off it. In castles they have tapestries to stop it bouncing.

questions.question: Is the reason for earthquakes or the increase in earthquakes around the world due to the fact that we're extracting oil from earth? Is oil like earth's natural lubricant, so now the tectonic plates can't smoothly glide against each other and instead grind and scrape causing earthquakes?

answers.answer: No.

questions.question: I told a joke to a woman recently and was accused of being a misogynist. Is there an equivalent word for women who hate men?

answers.answer: Missandrist (misandry). Misogyny means hatred of women, misandry means hatred of men. Misandrist is the female version.
Feminist.

questions.question: In the Bible, you have Mary Magdalene, Judas Iscariot, Pontius Pilate, John the Baptist - why do some biblical people have surnames (or what looks like surnames) while all the disciples are just known by one name?

answers.answer: Magdalene is a reference to a place - like Jesus of Nazareth. Judas out of Iscariot - Iscariot would be the area he came from. Many had their occupations as identifiers (Peter the Fisherman). Surnames were originally based on occupation or place of origin.

questions.question: I have a wheat and gluten-free diet. Why is it so much more expensive to buy things without wheat or gluten in them compared to things that contain it?

answers.answer: Supply and demand. Fewer customers mean higher prices. It costs much more to process the food and market it than for the massive majority of the population who are untroubled by the presence of gluten in their wheat-based products. As more people adopt gluten-free diets, prices will come down.

questions.question: Why do so many American state names end in an A?

answers.answer: It's an origin in Latin and Spanish. Most of the state names that are indigenous American names also end in A. But all the English names like Georgia, Carolina, Virginia are rooted from Latin, and Latin ends in A because it's a female name. The Spanish one is from Arabic. The two civilizations that colonized most of America used the female form IA and I-A.

questions.question: Why are there no queendoms, but they're all kingdoms?

answers.answer: Kings outrank queens. You only ever have a queen when there isn't an available king. A kingdom will always revert to a king when a king is available. Queens were only ever going to be on thrones that had been instituted and usually occupied by men. When the available bloodline of men was not available, it went to a queen until the next available man was there.

questions.question: How does the Wii Fit know what she had the night before / do something about multivitamins?

answers.answer: The Wii Fit is pre-programmed. When you switch it on, it gives you advice. It's a coincidence that she took multivitamins the day before and it came up with that advice. It's the same as saying you need so many hours sleep or don't do this.

questions.question: Where did the phrase 'belt and braces' come from?
Why does a biscuit absorb water slower when the tea is very hot, compared to when it's cooled down?
Why do royal statements come from St. James's Palace rather than Buckingham Palace?

answers.answer: It depends where the relevant royal resides. Statements about the Queen come from Buckingham Palace. Statements from Prince Charles would come from St. James's Palace.

The court of St. James is the oldest place. If you're an ambassador, you are accredited to the Court of St. James. That's where all royal pronouncements come from, whoever they involve. St. James's Palace predates all other royal residences - it was originally a leper's hospital for 13 virtuous leprous maidens, then made into a hunting lodge for Henry VIII.

questions.question: Why do front doors in Britain open inwards, while in Barbados they open outwards?

answers.answer: In Britain, doors open inwards so you don't knock over a passing pedestrian on the pavement.

It's a Victorian throwback and a manners or privacy thing. A room should always receive you. With internal doors, they always open inwardly. If you enter a room and the door opens outwards, you could catch people unawares and get a full picture of the room before they see you. It gives people margin of time.

questions.question: When you write a large amount on only one side of a piece of paper, it curls noticeably. Why does this happen and would writing on the other side curl it back?

answers.caller: Jill from the Isle of Wight
answers.answer: When paper is made, it's dried on enormous drums. This gives all paper a natural curl. When you write on it, the pressure and dampness makes the paper curl. When you turn over and write on the other side, because you've already followed the natural curl, it won't come back the same - you'll see a lesser curl because the action of writing stretches it.

questions.caller: David from London/Norfolk (Wormegay St Mary Magdalene)
questions.question: Do orbs in photographs really exist and are they from the spirit world?

answers.answer: Two points: 1) Strange lights at night are probably will-o'-the-wisp, caused by decaying organic matter. You only see them in the middle of nowhere. 2) Seeing faces in orbs is pareidolia - the brain tries to make sense of random data by assigning it to images we're familiar with. Example: 20 years ago there was a 'face on Mars' from low-resolution images. Later high-resolution photos proved it was just hills and shadows. Our brain sees patterns that aren't there.

questions.question: Why is the emergency number 999 when on a rotary phone, nine and zero take the longest to dial?

answers.answer: The metal stop at the bottom of the dial is next to the nine, so you can find it by feel in the dark.

Long ago, telephone poles had wires that would short out when wind blew them together, causing pulses of one. With 111 as emergency number, this would clog up the service. So they chose 999 to avoid accidental emergency calls.

questions.question: Do builders still put coins in the eaves of new-built houses?
Why are the four big tennis tournaments known as Grand Slam events?

answers.answer: It's probably from bridge/cards - when you win every trick in bridge it's called a slam. The term came from cards to tennis.

questions.question: What's the difference between single cream and double cream?

answers.answer: Double cream is called double cream because it has twice the fat content of single cream. Single cream is 18% fat, double cream is 36%.

questions.question: Why is going bananas synonymous with going crazy or berserk?
Why can't vacuum cleaner hoses reach all the way up stairs? Why don't they make them longer?

answers.answer: She uses Dysons professionally and just completed a job with 15 stairs using the extension and attachment that reached 16 steps.

Hoover is a trade name, not a verb. They invented the double-stretch hose in the 1950s before Dyson was born. It fitted onto the front or back of the machine and reached from bottom to top of stairs. It was a Hoover patent. Dyson now has his own device that does the same thing.

questions.question: Would a loaf of bread or piece of fruit still rot if sent up into the vacuum of space?

answers.caller: James from Streatham (caller with science degree)
answers.answer: If a person died in space without a spacesuit, there'd be some initial decomposition from intestinal bacteria. But you'd freeze pretty quickly, essentially becoming a freeze-dried mummy. Then decomposition would halt completely. It may still break down from solar radiation but that's not really decomposing, and the bacteria would die because it couldn't respirate.

questions.question: Why do we cut runner beans on a diagonal?

answers.answer: It increases surface area so more bean comes into direct contact with the hot water, cooking more effectively. Runner beans have a thick exterior, so diagonal cutting maximizes interior contact with heat.

questions.question: Why do some people say 'Well, I never'?

answers.answer: They haven't finished the sentence. 'Well, I never' really means 'Well, I never would have believed it' or 'Well, I never would have thought that could happen.' They're just saying half the sentence.

questions.question: Why doesn't rainwater flood down his chimney that's been open to the elements for 25 years?

answers.answer: The top of the chimney is small enough to let out smoke but not let in much water. The brick is absorbent, your house is warm. If you leave a 2-litre pop bottle out in torrential rain, barely any water collects at the bottom. The amount of rain entering a chimney is negligible and easily absorbed or evaporated.

Chimney flues are not built straight - they have a kink to help draw smoke out. Even if you threw half a bucket of water down there, most of it would go around the flue and be soaked up by the soot and dust. There's absorption, evaporation, and disfutation.

questions.question: Why is traditional mixer tonic water only available in 1-litre bottles when you can buy Coke in 2-litre bottles?

answers.answer: It's a simple question of demand. Most people don't use mixers to slake thirst - they use them to mix with spirits, so you don't need much and aren't going to sink a litre in a sitting. Tonic water loses its fizz over time, so nobody wants 2 litres. Ginger ale and ginger beer are more popular as straight drinks, hence bigger bottles. Nobody turns up at a corner shop wanting a can of tonic water to slake their thirst.

questions.question: Why is it when you're in a relationship, women are interested, but the moment you become single, there's not much interest?

answers.answer: Women are complicated and sophisticated. When you're not remotely interested in them, they take it as a challenge and are interested in you. When you're single and giving off sexual hunger vibes, she's picking up on it and refusing to feed you.

questions.question: Why do fingertips wrinkle if you stay in the bath for a long time?

answers.answer: Osmosis. The bath is wetter than the boy, and there's water going into the skin through a semipermeable membrane from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration. The wrinkling is liquid coming out of the skin.

questions.question: Is there a connection between camping (living in tents outdoors) and being camp (effeminate behavior)?
Why do we rely on signatures as security when they don't even expose a person's gender? Why don't we improve the system?

answers.answer: It's the least bad option available. Signatures are unreliable but what else would you use? Putting a little sticker with your face on every contract you ever signed isn't practical.

questions.question: Answer to why we say 'going bananas'

answers.answer: Have you ever seen a straight banana? They're all around the bend. That's why going bananas means going crazy - because bananas are naturally curved.

questions.question: How do they determine the temperature of the sun? I've read that they can say it's 20 million degrees Fahrenheit.
Why does white hair or grey hair grow faster than regular hair?
Where does Sylvania come from? (Pennsylvania is named after William Penn, so where does Sylvania come from?)

answers.answer: Sylvania comes from the Latin word sylvis or sylva for woodland. It just means a wooded land.

questions.question: Why, if you cut the palm of your hand, does it not produce a scab?

answers.answer: Skin's too thin. Or possibly too thick.
The constant movement of your hand stops a scab from forming.

questions.question: Why do pigeons never seem to nest in trees? They're always on buildings or under bridges.
If foxes chase and kill and eat chickens, why don't they do the same with pigeons?

We keep being told we're within six feet of a rat at any time, but why don't we ever see any rats when there are flash floods and rivers burst their banks? We never see them alive, dead, or trying to escape.
When and where did the term midwife originate?
Why do some mammals give birth standing up and their offspring land on their feet and can almost walk immediately, while humans give birth laying down head first and can't walk?

answers.answer: All mammals come out head first. The reason animals can walk immediately is evolution. Humans don't have to because we have nurturing mothers.

questions.question: Answer about pigeons nesting in trees

answers.answer: They do nest in trees. I was quoting a job in Slough and saw a pigeon's nest in a cedar tree. In the 14 years I've been running my business, we come across them quite regularly.

questions.question: Answer about pigeons nesting in trees

answers.answer: Pigeons do nest in trees, but the feral pigeon or flying rat is actually called a rock dove. Its natural habitat is to nest in cliffs and rock faces. As we've built towns and cities over the years, we've just given them a natural cliff face and a habitat. Seagulls are now becoming part of a similar phenomenon, as are peregrine falcons in cities.

questions.question: What's the point of the grills on the green light of traffic lights? Some have them, some don't.
Why can we hear people fishing across a lake from a distance, but across a field we wouldn't hear them at all?

answers.answer: Water has a smooth surface that allows sound waves to travel uninterrupted and not dissipate. Fields have countless tiny obstacles that block sound. It's like the Whispering Gallery at St. Paul's.

questions.question: Why do dogs like rolling in horse, fox, and other animal poo?
How does a leather strap sharpen a cutthroat razor? The leather is softer than the metal, so you can't scratch anything with leather.

answers.answer: A knife edge after use gets a slight burr - the tip of the cutting edge can fold over slightly. On a cutthroat razor with such thin metal, the leather strap, without doing any damage to the cutting edge, will bring that burr to the centre or get it off. So it isn't sharpening, it's restoring. To actually sharpen, you need an oilstone or whetstone.

questions.question: Answer about traffic light grills

answers.answer: The grills are so the motorist doesn't read another green light ahead and break red lights. Also, the sun sometimes cancels out the light - the sun can reflect on the green and make the driver behind think it's green when it's not. The grills prevent this.

questions.question: How do hurricanes get their names and who chooses them?

answers.answer: The American Meteorological Office names them. They're named in alphabetical order, chosen by the people that work there. They alternate between girls and boys names, or the scale of the storm determines whether it's male or female.

questions.question: Answer about why we don't see rats during floods

answers.answer: The brown rat (Rattus norvegicus) has very acute hearing. It hears when something is going to happen and will flee very quickly. They're also very good swimmers and burrowers. They peg it out of the pipes before the flood and then hide. Otherwise they'd get battered by humans or foxes. Some weaker ones do drown, but generally they move before anything happens.

questions.question: Answer about the origin of the word midwife

answers.answer: Midwife derives from Middle English. The word 'mid' is another word for 'with'. So it comes from Saxon origin, mit with, meaning 'with wife'. It just means the woman who is with the wife. And it doesn't have to be a woman - the person who is with the wife.

questions.question: On Top Gear, the presenters were driving along a public highway and chatting on CB radios, so they must be legal. But you have to look at mobile phones. So why are CB radios legal but mobile phones aren't?
Answer about how they determine the temperature of the sun

answers.answer: The Hubble telescope can measure in ultraviolet light how hot planets are, even far away ones. You point the Hubble at the sun and can calculate its temperature because of the ultraviolet rays. The Hubble has different spectrums - microwaves, ultraviolet rays - to see stuff beyond human eyes.

questions.question: Answer about CB radios

answers.answer: I used to be very friendly with a lorry driver who told me that CB radios are an earpiece. [Answer was interrupted]

questions.question: I'd like to know the origin of the statement, Get off Scott 3

answers.answer: Scott is an old word for a tax
Scott was an old name for window tax. The art of Scotting was boarding up your windows so you had fewer windows to be taxed on. A Scott-free house would be a house with no windows

Scott is a synonym for tax, derived from old Middle English 'Escot' from Scandinavia. In the Middle Ages, your drinking bill was kept on a slate called a Scot, and if you left without paying for your drink, you would be going Scot free

questions.question: Why do dogs have seven years to hour one? (Why dog years?)

answers.answer: It humanises the total - if you said a dog was 16, no one would think it was old
Dogs grow much quicker than a human. When they get to a year, they are seven years old

questions.question: Why is French kissing called French kissing?
Where do the germs go when you wash your hands? Do they drown? Do they die? And what's the point if they're back again straight away?

answers.answer: When you wash hands with water, you kill 50% of germs. Friction washes them away. With normal soap, you get to 90%. With a full hand scrub using Hibiscus or iodine, you get to 99.9%. Dettol only works on gram-negative bacteria, one of the main groups

questions.question: Why don't bats fall off their perches when they fall asleep? When they relax, why don't their feet unfurl?

answers.answer: It works the opposite way for bats. Their feet naturally close and they stay in that position - they have to make the effort to open them to let go. More like a clamp than a hook

questions.question: What happens to the rubber that wears off car tyres? Why aren't we all wading in inches of rubber?

answers.answer: It turns into dust and gets washed away by rain and goes down drains. Same as skin

questions.question: Every night around 5:30, hundreds of starlings perch on power cables facing the same direction. Why?

answers.answer: They're roosting. David Lindo, the urban birder, told me this. Birds gather socially to roost but don't nest there. Like the ring-tailed parakeets at Wormwood Scrubs
He accepts James's explanation about roosting but notes the follow-up question about WHY they roost remains unanswered

questions.question: Why does Barcelona have Saint George on their club logo since they're Spanish?

answers.answer: Saint George is the patron saint of lots of places including England, Georgia, Egypt, Bulgaria, and Catalonia. Barcelona is based in Catalonia, so the flag of St George is on their shirt because he's the patron saint of Catalonia
Barcelona was formed by English, Spanish, and Swiss men - this is mentioned by Martin Tyler in FIFA 12

questions.question: Why are vanilla pods black when vanilla ice cream is white? Strawberry is strawberry-colored, chocolate is chocolate-colored. Why isn't vanilla black?

answers.answer: The vanilla flavor dissipates throughout the cream but the color doesn't. You need a tiny pinch of vanilla for an epic flavor kick - so little it doesn't affect color. Strawberry and chocolate need much more quantity to achieve similar flavor strength, so they affect the color. Cheap vanilla ice cream often has no actual vanilla in it. Mint ice cream is green because of food coloring

questions.question: Every time we strip out buildings and dig into foundations, we find a silver spoon. Why is there a silver spoon in the foundations of all these homes?
When I fill my empty fridge freezer with new food, will it use more energy?

answers.answer: When you put unfrozen food in, the temperature rises, the thermostat triggers the compressor to run until it cools everything back down. During that period, yes, it works harder
Fridges run cheaper when full. Cold air sinks out every time you open the door, and replaced by warm air. The less air in the fridge, the cheaper to run
Her fridge manual says if your fridge is full, it has to work twice as hard. But you shouldn't fill it completely to capacity either - it costs more if overfilled

questions.question: Why are cherries always the lowest prize on fruit machines, when cherries are an expensive fruit?
Why do they dim the cabin lights when landing at night? Surely more light is safer?

answers.answer: Two reasons: one, it helps your eyes acclimatise to the gloom if you have to evacuate. Two, landing and taking off is when aircraft are most at risk. If there's an engine fire, with lights dimmed and blinds up, it's easier for cabin crew to identify it and know which side of the aircraft it's on, so they can position the aircraft to evacuate the other side

questions.question: Why does my body give me hot flushes? Everyone says it's my hormones but nobody can tell me what my body is trying to do
What do vegetarians feed their pets, dogs or cats?

answers.answer: Cats cannot be fed vegetarian food - they need meat or they will die. As a vegetarian myself, I feed my cat meat-based food because it's only fair to the cat. You have to draw a line between your principles and practical animal care.

questions.question: Why do people who have had a heavy night's sleep look puffy around the eyes? What makes a heavy night's sleep different to any other?

answers.answer: The better your night's sleep, the more tired you can be in the morning because you've spent longer in deep sleep and released more sleep-related hormones or endorphins. There may be a relationship between eye puffiness and the amount of endorphins released.
When you don't get much REM sleep, you blink less, so you get more fluid retention and puffy eyes. The skin falling the night before contributes to this fluid retention.

questions.question: What would happen if you were driving down a motorway at 70 miles per hour and then quickly pulled it into reverse?

answers.answer: The car won't let you do it. There's a mechanism that stops you from going into reverse when the car is moving forward. You just grind it - it won't happen. This only works going from fifth gear to first gear. From neutral you can crunch into any gear.

questions.question: What does 'I'd give my IT for something' mean?
Why do we say 'excuse my French' after using profanity? Where does this come from?

answers.answer: Beards are rebellious - after the Norman conquest, English people grew beards to demonstrate their Saxon credentials and show they weren't buying into the fancy mincing foreign ways of Frenchmen.

questions.question: What is the little hook on the end of a McDonald's ice cream spoon for?

answers.answer: The hook holds the spoon straight in the McFlurry machine while it's stirring. The McFlurry is made by putting ice cream in the pot, adding a topping, inserting the spoon and then inserting the whole thing into a machine to stir it up. It's a multi-purpose spoon - both spoon and stirrer.

questions.question: Why do all fire escape spiral staircases turn the same way (anticlockwise going down)?

answers.answer: If you go back to the days of Romans and castles, you'd be defending from the top down if you were being attacked. Most people are right-handed, so you have the advantage coming down to hold the balance on your left and use the sword on your right. Coming up, attackers had to use their left hand, which was a disadvantage. The spiral stairs were designed as a nuisance for attackers.

Fire escapes are essentially planted on a building after it's been built as an afterthought to meet modern legislation. The likelihood of being able to put an extra banister on the outside is much lower than if you were building from scratch. Your flat's spiral fire escape does go clockwise going down, which would be quite clumsy if you're right-handed unless you've got a banister on the outside. I work in the security and fire alarm industry.

questions.question: Why does the train toilet sign say 'do not flush while the train is stationary'?

answers.answer: Because it all goes on the tracks.

Older style trains like old slam door trains used to dump material directly on the tracks, which is why the placards were there. But newer trains have different legislation - it gets collected into a big tank underneath and then when trains go back to the depot at the end of the evening, someone empties those tanks. If Sarah saw signs in Sheffield, she may be on an old-fashioned train. I'm a pilot and I write computer games, so I spend time around trains and railway depots.

questions.question: Why is it called a booby trap?

answers.answer: Booby is a bird that frequents the sea and makes very good eating. In years gone by, fishermen, pirates and buccaneers used to set traps for the booby to catch it and eat it. Boobies are easy to catch - they fly like albatrosses. The blue-footed booby is a specific type. Because the bird was easily duped or lured into a trap, the word became synonymous with something that was easily caught, hence 'booby trap'. I'm ex-military and used to have to explain this to recruits.

questions.question: Who decides who goes on banknotes and is there a pecking order?
Why do I need 5-7 speakers for surround sound when I only have two ears?

answers.answer: Sound comes from 360 degrees around you. The more speakers you've got, the more realistic that field will become. If you've only got one speaker, it sounds like it's coming from a speaker. With lots of speakers, you increase the field of sound feeding your ears so it sounds like you're in the room. Your ear is like a microphone but it's wired to your brain, which calculates where the noise is coming from based on the information both ears provide.

questions.question: What is the little P in the corner of TV programmes like Deal or No Deal?

answers.answer: The P signifies that this programme has product placement in it. It started with Coronation Street and Big Bubba. Things that aren't blurred out - brands and logos - indicate product placement. On Big Bubba they have blatant close-ups of Morrison's products.

questions.question: Why have they changed the Olympic podium so that silver and bronze are now at the same level, when years ago bronze was always lower than silver?

answers.answer: In the Olympic medal table, the only thing that seems to count where you come in a table is gold, so I would guess that reflects the same thinking - making silver and bronze equal emphasizes that only gold really matters.

questions.question: When a cuckoo lays its eggs in another bird's nest and that cuckoo is raised by a completely different species, how does it know it's a cuckoo when it leaves the nest? How does it know to mate with other cuckoos?

answers.answer: The only thing I can think is that it's to do with the distinctive call. A duck raised by people tends to think it's a human being, but it's not going to want to mate with you. How does a cuckoo know it's a cuckoo? Because it says cuckoo all the time. As soon as it opens its mouth and starts going cuckoo, it knows what it is. I can't help the noise it makes any more than a baby can help making baby noises.

questions.question: Why in the Olympic stadiums do they use lanes 2 to 9? What's wrong with lane 1?

answers.answer: The innermost lane has such an acute curvature that the sprinter wouldn't be able to accelerate - they have to eliminate man-made drag factors. In a sprint, particularly in the 200 and 400, you use lanes 2 to 9 so no one is really leaning. In long distance races it doesn't matter because the pace is slower. Lane 1 exists because long distance runners don't have the same acceleration issue.

questions.question: If a flying ant lands on my windscreen and I drive 5 miles up the road and it's still alive and it flies off, will it be able to make its way back to the nest?

answers.answer: Once inseminated, the queen never goes back home - the whole point of flying ants is that the female who's going to be the queen of the next ant nest flies up as high as she can, the strongest male gets to her, inseminates her, then she comes down and makes her nest. The males only have one function and they never go back home.

questions.question: Why are midges confined to the highlands of Scotland? What keeps them there and stops them spreading?

answers.answer: The gnat hole is wet, very peaty. That's probably why you'll find a lot of them in the Highlands. You'll find them absolutely anywhere that's just rural and wet - it's meteorological and geographical conditions that are just particularly prevalent in those parts. That's why you'll never find them in a city centre.

questions.question: Why can I always smell burnt toast on the train between Waterloo and Clapham Junction? It's on different trains going different places but always on that route.

answers.answer: It's at the railway arches just near Vauxhall station - there's a Costa coffee depot where they roast the coffee. The smell just happens to be detected as burnt toast by the brain but it's actually coffee roasting.

He was four metres from the Jubilee line, 31 metres underground, and the same question was asked yesterday. They had just burnt their toast and the extractor fans were taking the smell out onto the platform.

questions.question: Is there a limit to pain?

answers.answer: Everyone has a different threshold. Athletes particularly - marathon runners and rowers can endure more pain than average people. Everybody eventually reaches a point where they'd pass out from pain. The message from the brain to the body would be shut down. So yes it would go up forever until you pass out, but it's different for different people - there's no objective maximum pain threshold.

questions.question: Why is a stroke called a stroke?

answers.answer: It comes from the Greek word 'apoplexy' which means 'struck down'. It happens suddenly - if you've had a stroke you've been struck down.
Stroke is a cerebrovascular accident, CVA. It happens so quick, it happens in a stroke - literally comes from the word stroke, not apoplexy.

questions.question: Why do we get dark rings around our eyes when we're tired?
If you gathered up all the money in the world and shared it among everyone, how much would each person get?

answers.answer: Rough estimate would be about 500 quid per person if you divided the currency in the world between the population.

questions.question: If the royal family and parliament were wiped out, who would take over and run the country?

answers.answer: There's an enormously long line of succession, plus royals don't rule the country - they just ratify it. If every single member of parliament was wiped out, the civil service would step into the breach, you'd have elections, you'd fill it up again the next day.

questions.question: Dogs wag their tails when they're happy. Do horses do anything to show happiness and do they know when they've had a good run?

answers.answer: You can tell what horses are thinking and feeling mainly by their ears but also their tails. When horses are working hard and concentrating, their ears will be flat back. When they go over the line and know they've won, their ears flick forward. When you're riding and talking to your horse, their ears go backwards and forwards and twitch - they're listening and communicating. The ears are the best giveaway. If a horse's ears are flicking and tail is flicking, he's probably not happy - he's irritated. When a horse is really sad, his ears flop out to the side, eyes look dull, body language hunches up.

questions.question: Why is it the Royal Navy, yes the Royal Air Force, yes not the Royal Army regiments?

answers.answer: The army is a collection of regiments - many of which are royal like the Royal Fusiliers and Royal Engineers. The army is an umbrella organization containing royal regiments. The RAF and Navy are more self-contained with squadrons and divisions rather than separate regiments.

questions.question: Why do I sneeze so loudly? My dad does too so there must be a genetic link.

answers.answer: He used to be a loud sneezer. When he went to the doctors complaining it hurt when he sneezed, they told him to empty his lungs when he feels a sneeze coming on - that's the fuel to the explosion. If you breathe in, you'll do an enormous sneeze. If you consciously exhale, you'll do a nice little delicate sneeze.

questions.question: Does lemon-scented washing up liquid actually smell like lemons?

answers.answer: When you smell it, you won't smell lemons - you'll smell oranges. Lemon-scented products contain orange, not lemon.

questions.question: Why are there so few poisonous animals in the UK?

answers.answer: What is the first thing humans do when they colonise an area? They get rid of threats - they're the ultimate predator, at the top of most food chains. Wherever humankind is most populous, threats to humankind will be most diminished. Climate also plays a role - venomous creatures are more suited to tropical climates. If the jungle was hugely populated, humans would have got rid of the dangerous creatures.

There's a distinction - 'poisonous' means what you ingest, 'venomous' means what is injected. There are loads of poisonous animals like the black widow spider and wolf spider. Venomous animals used to be here but they've been killed off - predators were introduced that killed them all. Humans don't want to live near things that can kill them, so they've been husbandried to safety.

questions.question: How do Olympic cyclists take comfort breaks during those long road races? I didn't see them stop.

answers.answer: They can either pull over to the side of the road and do their business, or if they're with teammates, the teammates will group around them and he'll whip it out and do it while cycling. In the Olympic road race, the camera actually showed them pulling over and doing their wee on the side of the road. In the triathlon you've already been for a swim so it doesn't matter. Or they can go in the saddle.

questions.question: What's stronger - a house made from shredded wheat or a house made from Weetabix?

answers.answer: Weetabix would be less susceptible to rain and have higher density.
Shredded wheat would be stronger - it's manufactured as a structured product, designed to be a structure. The other stuff goes soggy in the bowl.

questions.question: Why can you cook frozen chicken from frozen if it's in a prepared meal, but you need to defrost chicken if you buy it separately?

answers.answer: The pre-prepared chicken pack is already cooked, so the bacteria have been killed. The chicken he buys separately is raw and needs to be defrosted thoroughly to cook out all the bacteria.

questions.question: How long would it take to fill an empty glass with dust?

answers.answer: Dust is electrically charged, which is why it settles on surfaces. If dust was landing on dust and any breeze existed, it would disperse it. You could never have a glass full of dust in any normal environmental circumstances because the charge required wouldn't allow it to settle.

In power stations that burn rubbish, dust builds up to one to two inches every six months at high levels. However, this is freakish circumstances - they even spray water inside to keep dust levels down.

questions.question: Why are the last three characters of number plates blacked out on transporters carrying second-hand cars?

answers.answer: It's to do with ANPR cameras. Even on the back of a truck, the cameras will ping up for no insurance or no tax, and it stops them getting pulled over.

The cars are salvaged, basically from vehicle crime. They're written off with no insurance. When the plate goes through the camera, it pings up with no insurance and no tax. Covering the plates stops them getting pulled over. Nothing to do with cloning.

questions.question: Why are beach volleyball and handball Olympic events when they don't seem like endurance sports?

answers.answer: Endurance is not the key criteria for Olympic sports. The Olympic motto is 'faster, higher, stronger.' Beach volleyball and handball are Olympic sports and that's why they're included.

questions.question: Is it dangerous to mix fish and yogurt?
Why are the Olympics using BMW cars instead of British cars?

answers.answer: There is no British-owned car company manufacturing vehicles suitable for the job. Jaguar is now Indian-owned (Tata), and BMW is built in Britain by British workers. The Olympics is international.

BMW is one of the Olympic Games partners, like Coca-Cola, McDonald's, Adidas, and EDF. They paid huge amounts of money to be Olympic sponsors. They support the Olympics and contribute to volunteering and other costs. Jaguar and other brands didn't want it enough or aren't under contract.

questions.question: Why do they search boxers' flesh before a bout?

answers.answer: They check the gloves, tap the front of shorts to ensure foul-proof protector is in place, and check for excessive vaseline. Too much grease causes cuts because the gloves abrade the skin. They also wipe off excess water which would minimize friction and affect punch landing, plus prevent slipping in the ring. Qualifications: helped run one of the top amateur boxing clubs in the country.

questions.question: Why do we say 'par boiled' instead of 'part boiled'?

answers.answer: Parboiling is an abbreviation of the word 'partial.' You don't want a 'part-boiled' potato which would mean it's raw in places, like a curate's egg. 'Partially boiled' means it has been partially boiled.

questions.question: Why is the swimming event called 'freestyle' when it's always front crawl?

answers.answer: It's called freestyle so they can continue to search for new ways of swimming. If someone developed a new faster stroke, it could be used in freestyle.

The clue is in the name. Freestyle means literally whatever is the fastest way to get through the water. The other three strokes have specific standards. If someone in doggy paddle was faster than front crawl, they could use it. Qualifications: was a competitive swimmer at county level.

questions.question: How many positions can a GPS satellite register at one time?

answers.answer: The question is void. GPS doesn't quite work that way. Wherever you are on planet Earth, you can always see at least three GPS satellites, and they're all broadcasting the same signal continuously. Your device measures signal strength from each one to determine position. There are quite a lot of GPS satellites in total.

questions.question: Why do female tennis players use 'Miss' at Wimbledon but not at the Olympics?

answers.answer: The Lawn Tennis Association sets the rules for Wimbledon, and the International Olympic Committee sets the rules for the Olympics. Men at Wimbledon aren't called Mr. Smith either - they just use surnames. Blokes can't be anything but mister, while ladies have options: miss, missus, or miz.

questions.question: With regard to the Olympic bid, what do countries pay for? Do they pay their own airfare? Or how do poor countries like Cameroon come to the Olympics? Who pays the athletes' airfares, hotels, and getting here and back?

answers.answer: I have absolutely no idea. That's why it's called the Mystery Hour. We provide their accommodation in the Olympic Village, but we don't pay for their flight.
Not provided in transcript

questions.question: When you're abroad, you can't drink the tap water, yet you can eat the local produce - vegetables and fruits - which have often been watered with that same tap water. Why is that safe?

answers.answer: The water in a watermelon is organic and has been chemically transformed through the plant's growth. It's not the same water you sprinkled on the garden. The process is called growing.
The initial absorption of the root is through a semi-permeable membrane, and that leads to osmosis. Only pure water passes through - the contamination is left behind. It's a process of filtration.

questions.question: When we start off as one cell, two cells, four, eight, sixteen - all the way up - what's the first recognisably human thing that develops? Is it a skull, an organ?

answers.answer: The heart develops first. Everything else develops around the heart because it needs blood supply. The heart develops, then blood vessels, then it turns into different organs, bone structure, nervous system, and brain.

questions.question: Why do we celebrate everything with a cake? Birthday cake, Christmas cake. Why not a donut or hamburger? Why cake?

answers.answer: Cake contains the most luxurious ingredients in the contemporaneous larder - flour, eggs, milk, sugar, chocolate, cream, fruit. That's why cake denotes celebration historically.

questions.question: Why do we feel sleepy or tired when we get warm? When I'm driving around I feel really sleepy because I'm warm, and that happens at home too.

answers.answer: Blood flows around the body helped by salt particles joined together by platelets. When you get warm, the salt leaves the body through sweat. As the blood loses its helper (salt), it goes slower around the body and you get lethargic. I was a Chief Pediatrics and Physical Training Instructor in the Royal Navy.

questions.question: Why are the Olympics called London 2012 when so many events aren't actually in London? Like women's football in Cardiff. Why not call it UK or Great Britain 2012? Why do they only have one city bid when no city could host everything?

answers.answer: Tradition - it's the host city. The city that bids, hosts it. Since 1896, they've named it after the host city. You can't have the Olympics in one city only - even Los Angeles used Santa Barbara for some events. No city could provide all facilities.

questions.question: Three questions in one - What do the Olympic rings represent? Why five? And why are they entwined?

answers.answer: The five Olympic rings represent the five big inhabited continents. They're linked together to show they're coming together for a worldwide event. There are five different colors (red, blue, green, black, yellow) because every single flag in the world has at least one of those colors in it. I learned this doing an Olympics project at school. I'm nine years old.

questions.question: How do they time the speed of a ball at the Wimbledon tennis tournament? When you watch on TV they say it traveled at 193 miles per hour or 50 miles per hour.

answers.answer: They use a low-powered radar transmitter, like police radar guns. As the ball travels towards it or away from it, it causes a Doppler shift. The receiver picks up the shift in frequency and calculates the speed. I was an ex-Royal Naval weapons engineer specialising in radar guidance systems. Now I fix microwaves.

questions.question: Prince Charles's toast from his honeymoon got sold last week. How has it managed to stay fresh for 30 years? How has it maintained its freshness and not get moldy?

answers.answer: They put it in a paper, then in a plastic bag and stuck it in the freezer. I have some 10-year-old wedding cake in my freezer that still looks like wedding cake.
Requested a Steward's Inquiry to verify

questions.question: On eight Summer Olympics they add a new event. Why is that and who chooses what event it should be?

answers.answer: They change things around in subjective disciplines (marked by judges). Golf is coming in. BMX biking. Tennis has come and gone and come back. I tried to get darts introduced but it didn't work. The decisions are made by the Olympic committee.

questions.question: Tattoos - why don't they disappear? Your skin renews itself, you haven't got 100-year-old skin, so surely the tattoo should be covered up. Even if the needle goes deep, you should have seven layers of skin over the top.

answers.answer: When tattoo ink is injected under the skin, the immune system tries to attack it as a foreign body. Because the ink globules are too large, the immune system forms a collagen ring around each globule to isolate it. Once isolated, the immune system stops attacking. That's why it's permanent. For removal, lasers shatter the ink globules into tiny fragments, re-releasing them into the body. The immune system attacks what it can, but remaining large pieces get new collagen rings. It's a fading process like the game Asteroids. I own a tattoo removal clinic on Harley Street - I've been doing this for 15 years.

questions.question: Why is government legislation called a white paper? Why not something else?

answers.answer: The green paper was the consultation document. The white paper means it's finished and going forward as legislation. Different colored papers in Parliament signal the status of the proposal.

questions.question: No question - provided answers in advance: 1) Ants have little hairs on their feet. 2) It was during the Great Fire of London. 3) From 1896 to 1904. 4) Difference in air pressure from one to ten. 5) Osmosis.
On a podium at Olympic ceremonies when they're giving out medals, why is it that combination? Third place on the right-hand side, second on the left, first in the middle. Why that arrangement?
Why is green associated with jealousy?

answers.answer: From Shakespeare - Iago says it to Othello: 'Beware my lord of jealousy, it is the green-eyed monster that doth mock the meat it feeds on.' But going back further, the Greeks associated colours with emotions. If you were red, you were angry. If you were blue, you were something else. And envy was very much associated with green because it was seen as a sickness. If you felt envious, you felt sick. There's a reference in Sappho dating back to the 7th century BC.

questions.question: Why are strawberries sold in a punnet, and is there any other fruit sold like it?

answers.answer: Soft fruit can be sold in punnets, but not by the punnet. They have to be sold by reference to weight. It's the Weights and Measures Act. Roadside sellers selling them in the punnet almost as a volumetric measure rather than weight - they have to be sold by weight.

questions.question: Children are told never to look at the sun because they'll go blind. How do animals know not to do this, or are they just more intelligent than us?

answers.answer: It's the same as fire. How does my cat know not to jump into the fire? Because he gets just close enough to appreciate the heat and realise that the closer he gets, the hotter it will be. How do they know not to stare at the sun? Because they look at it just enough to realise it can't possibly be doing them any good. It's uncomfortable. They can't focus properly afterwards, which makes them more vulnerable to prey. So they do it once or twice, and then they know never to do it again.

questions.question: When I was a kid I was always told that if you threw a penny off the Eiffel Tower, it had the force of a brick hitting the floor. Is that true?

answers.answer: I don't know. I think the answer is no, because you have terminal velocity. It doesn't matter where you drop something from, it hits terminal velocity. So if you've got a penny, will it reach its terminal velocity before hitting the ground from the Eiffel Tower? I don't know.

After a short while, a penny reaches its terminal velocity, which with the weight of a penny is well below any kind of force that could do any sort of damage. At the worst, it could just break skin. A brick would hurt because of its mass, but a penny would be terminal but not fatal.

questions.question: When I was a child I remembered my dad telling me that you had to be an amateur to take part in the Olympics. Is that true? And if so, when and why did athletes stop being amateurs?

answers.answer: Most of the sports were still amateur, but in athletics and track and field there was a growing professional circuit in the early 80s. I remember a documentary where Alan Wells was being poached onto it but he refused to turn pro. The IOC was afraid the Olympics would be lacking stars, so they changed their policy. Like when Rod Laver opted out of Wimbledon after turning pro in 1962. The first games where professionals were allowed was 1988 - that was the Carl Lewis era. They were the big stars for the Americas.

questions.question: How do cats get their markings? I've got a black and white cat and she's almost symmetrical. You get a litter of cats where you get a tabby cat, a black cat, or a dappled cat. But they look like they've been splashed with paint.
Why are insects attracted to ultraviolet light?

answers.answer: I think historically they fly towards the moon. They use the moon as a navigational aid, and maybe ultraviolet light is like a fake moon.

answers.caller: Emma from Dalston (beekeeper, father is entomologist)
answers.answer: Insects see in a higher spectrum than we do. They're drawn to ultraviolet light which is invisible to the human eye. Other insects are drawn to light bulbs because they're used to only having the moon as a source of light during the night. That's what they use as a navigational tool. Flowers emit ultraviolet light that the human eye can't see, so they're drawn to it as a source of food.

questions.question: When the Army is involved in security of the Olympics, will they be wearing their desert camouflage fatigues or a smarter uniform?

answers.caller: Pete from Dagenham (8 years in forces)
answers.answer: They will be wearing their day-to-day working dress, which is called DPM (Disruptive Pattern Material). The number ones and number twos (dress uniform with medals) are only worn on certain occasions and are too uncomfortable to work in. Only certain regiments like guards get number ones.

questions.question: In the Christian religion, which is more important, Westminster Abbey or St. Paul's Cathedral?

answers.answer: They're two branches of the Christian religion - Catholic and Protestant. To a Catholic, Westminster Cathedral (near Victoria) would be more important. To a Protestant, Canterbury would supersede Westminster. Prince William got married at Westminster Abbey, Prince Charles at St. Paul's.

They're about the same, but it depends. St. Paul's was built during the Protestant Reformation to rival St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Coronations take place at Westminster Abbey, which would swing it back the other way. There's not much between them.

questions.question: Where could you go outside the eurozone where you could actually spend euros? How far out of the eurozone can you realistically expect to use euros?

answers.answer: If you look on a euro note, there's a little map of Europe showing the countries it can be used. In the corner there's a little square representing French Guiana, which is in South America. That's one of the furthest away places you can use the euro.

France has overseas territories - the Antilles, St. Martin, Guadeloupe, etc. They are French departments, so the euro is legal tender there. They have mostly American tourists, so dollars are widely used out of pragmatism, but the basic prices are in euros.

questions.question: What is a sausage in a bed of batter called?

answers.answer: Toad in the hole.

questions.question: Why is Toad in the Hole called Toad in the Hole?

answers.caller: Barry from Southend (catering background, went to Caitlin College)
answers.answer: It was originally called frog in the hole - literally old peasant food. When it first got made, it was a cheap and easy meal. It wasn't actually sausage originally - could be any sort of variety of meat, even pigeon in the 1700s. You could hide the meat in the batter. The reason it got called toad in the hole is because when the rich saw frogs in ponds, they'd see little heads just popping up. The top of a sausage poking out of the batter looks like a frog's head.

questions.question: Why have we singled out the crow for flying in particularly perpendicular/straight lines? Does the crow fly any straighter than any other bird?

answers.answer: As the crow flies comes from nautical days when you were up in the crow's nest looking for land - you looked in straight lines, you didn't look around corners. So as the crow flies from the crow's nest is where the land was. That's why it's in straight lines.

questions.question: If a meteorite was heading towards Earth, what could we do to prevent it from hitting us? Are there official measures in place to cope with imminent arrival of a meteorite?

answers.answer: We're constantly bombarded by meteorites. Most burn up to some extent on entry and when they land they're no bigger than a golf ball. Most land in the sea. There are government research programs around the world spending millions. With regards to the likelihood of being hit by a large enough meteorite to be a human race killer, there are meteorites the size of the O2 around the world. The most likely way to change course would be a nuclear blast - if you hit it you'd smash it into thousands of pieces. To my limited knowledge, if one was large enough, the best we could hope for is to knock it off its course.

questions.question: When dogs stick their head out the window they love it. But when you blow in their face, they go doolally. Why?

answers.answer: Dogs pant to get fresh air through their nose and mouth to cool down. When they're in the car, they put their head out because it's free-flowing air so they don't have to use energy panting. When a human blows on their face, it's not free-flowing air, it's not fresh air for them. It's the same as when we have a fresh breeze come past us - it's pleasant. They like it because it's cooler and cleaner air, plus they don't have to pant.

questions.question: Where does the saying 'it's given me the heebie-jeebies' come from?
When I was 14, I put two caterpillars on my doorstep. When I came back six hours later, there were over 30. Does anybody know why?
Pet owners take cats and dogs for yearly vaccinations for up to about nine diseases. Why don't humans have yearly inoculations? Is it because we're bigger so the inoculations work longer?
Why is the time on every single watch displayed as 10 past 10 or 10 to 2? It's everywhere in magazines and shops.

answers.answer: The clock is smiling - which means you're more likely to buy it. Hence why it's not 20 past 7, because then it would be frowning. It conveys a happy, positive feeling.
The clock is set at 10 to 2 because that is the time that King Charles I was beheaded and he was a patron of clockmakers, so they set it at 10 to 2 to respect his death. It was about 6 minutes to 2.

questions.question: After watching Wimbledon, tennis balls are green. Yet every other sport played on grass has a different coloured ball. Why are tennis balls green?

answers.answer: The balls are not green - they're high-vis yellow (fluorescent yellow). Back in the 60s/70s when Wimbledon was played on grass, the game was different with gents and ladies coming to net more, so courts got worn out more. When the balls were white, you couldn't see the court wear on TV because frame rates weren't good. With improved television technology and the change in the nature of the game, yellow balls can be seen better both on TV and by spectators when the sun is shining.

questions.question: I bought a frosted glass table. When I put frozen things on it, the frost disappears and the table goes transparent. But underneath where the object was, it's wet. How does this happen? Is it osmosis?

answers.answer: The water on the underside is condensation - water from the air condensing on the cold surface (like on the inside of a windscreen). The frosting isn't really frosting - it's irregularities in the surface (like chips in the glass) that scatter light, creating the frosted appearance. When you put a frozen carton on it, fluid gets into the chips and freezes in a flat surface, allowing light to pass through directly, making it transparent until it warms up and becomes frosted again.

questions.question: Answer about dog vaccinations

answers.answer: If your dog has had all the puppy shots and the one they get at a year old, it's immune for life. Everything after that - the yearly reminder to come and get your pet immunized - is an absolute scam. Your pet's not being re-immunized because it's already immune. It's being over-medicated. This is controversial to the drug companies and the vets.
I can't let that be taken as advice by anybody. If my animals are sick, I'll go to the vet. And if I'm sick, I'll go to the doctor.

questions.question: On corporate clothing, why is the company logo always on the left-hand side on the chest?

answers.answer: Logos are on the left-hand side close to the heart - to convey sincerity for the company or organisation you work for. Especially with football clubs, you'll see the vast majority of shirts have their crest on the left breast.
The logo is on the left because our heart is there - it's pumping, you're looking at the force of gravity onto your heart. (This was an answer to the anti-clockwise running question.)

questions.question: How does a rechargeable toothbrush charge when there's no direct electrical connection between the toothbrush and the base station?

answers.answer: It's electromagnetic induction - you put the coil around the base station and it charges.
You've got a coil in the toothbrush and a magnet in the base unit. The magnet spins in the coil and creates a current in that coil which charges the battery up.

questions.question: In sporting events where competitors race around a track, why do they always race in an anti-clockwise direction?

answers.answer: Because our heart is on the left - your heart is pumping and you're looking at the force of gravity onto your heart. If you run the other way it could cause problems. In Australia they actually advise doing training going the opposite way so you won't hurt your left-hand side hip. Endurance runners often train the opposite way to even up their hips.

questions.question: What do the factors mean on suntan cream (Factor 10, 20, 30)? What do they do to the stuff inside to make it more of a factor?

answers.answer: It's just like the thickness, isn't it? How much UV way can get through it? But what did it actually do add to it to make it more... Or take away? I mean, so you start with factor 50 and then you dilute it according to how little you want, don't you? And then you end up with olive oil.

It's essentially a factor that tells you by what factor how long you can then be exposed to UV light. So it's a factor of two. You are half as less. It takes you double the time to get burned, as it were... it's just different quantities of mineral that covers the skin and therefore blocks out the UV light. So it's just different quantities of mineral that covers the skin and therefore blocks out... Yeah, like a full sunblock uses a very high quantity. Yes. And then it just dilutes. Until you get to oils and even less.

questions.question: If someone loses their legs and they're fitted with prosthetic legs, say he was 5 foot 6 and a doctor come round to measure you up, if you'd be allowed to say to him, could you make me 6 foot? Is there some sort of rule where they'd say, no, we've got to make you the height you was before?

answers.answer: I wouldn't have thought so, but it's balance. I mean, if you got used to walking before you lost your legs... They have to teach you to walk again anyway, don't they? But the centre of gravity would be different if you were shorter or smaller or taller.

questions.question: I was walking on my way to work at Old Street, looking in London black taxis, and realised none of them are wearing seatbelts. So why is it they're not obliged or don't have to wear seatbelts?

answers.answer: So that a passenger can't strangle them from behind and steal all their money... I'm 99% certain that that's the definitive answer, but only because I think we might have done it before.
We don't wear a seatbelt because we have to get out to assist passengers and load luggage into the vehicle on a regular basis.

It's nothing to do with health and safety... It's nothing to do with getting strangled from behind... It's one of those very old Hackney carriage acts that go back from the horse-drawn and all that sort of thing.

questions.question: The world has a magnetic field which diverts some of the harmful radiation which the sun spews out towards us into space. Does the Earth's magnetic field repel radiation away? And without the magnetic field, would life on Earth be possible?

answers.answer: Yeah, I'm pretty well sure... I think I know this... I'm just... Well read.

We would not exist if it would not be for the protection we get from the big iron core in the middle of the Earth that creates this magnetic shield around us. The Sun is throwing off huge amounts of radiation... Like an explosion would, like a nuclear explosion. It's a massive nuclear reactor. And it's throwing out all these particles and all this energy and there's nothing much in between us and the Sun. So, all these particles are flying towards us 93 million miles across space. If they were... If it wasn't for the magnetic shield we have, they would hit us and all the cells in our body and that would be rather like nuclear radiation and it would destroy parts of your DNA... You would get radiation sickness of sorts... You'd be getting the fallout. That's because it's all... It's part of electromagnetic spectrum. So, you've got this big magnetic field and a bit like, you know, old television sets... There was a big magnet in them. And it fired stuff out the back of the television and the magnet bent it round to make it big and hit the screen. Right. And the magnet is bending all of this... All of these particles flying at the screen. It's bending them. So, the magnet around the Earth bends this... What they call it, solar wind. This dangerous solar wind. It bends it around the Earth. And deflects it. It's a shield. The Earth actually has a sort of long sort of tail behind it where all this wind gets deflected. A bit like wind going round, you know, wind tunnels... Like an exhaust. And occasionally that tail gets too long and it snaps backwards. It kind of releases. And that's the field coming back again and that's where all the auroras boreali is on the North and South Pole.

questions.question: You can tell the age of the tree by the rings. If you cut the branch, would it tell you how old the branch is or how old the tree is?

answers.answer: It would tell you how old the branch was. It's how many years have passed since it started spouting, isn't it? So there's a ring for every year that it's spouted. So the branch comes out of the bough, the bough comes out of the tree. You'd have three different numbers of rings on the branch, the bough, and the tree... If I took my arm off... If you... Imagine... If five years from now what has become the bough of a tree branches out, that branch is not five years old. It can't have five years worth of rings inside it, can it? But the tree is that old. But you'd have to chop the whole tree down to count those rings. You chop the branch off, you can only find out how long the branch has been growing out of that bit of the tree.

questions.question: Which ones do the pecking? Is it the male or the females? If you want to tell the difference between them, then, like the rest of the bird kingdom, the one with the more impressive plumage will be the male. Are both male and female woodpeckers responsible for the pecking?

answers.answer: Why would it not be both of them? Yeah, because it wouldn't be a woodpecker, would it, otherwise? They've got to both. They've got to peck, otherwise it wouldn't be a woodpecker. And if you want to tell the difference between them, then, like the rest of the bird kingdom, the one with the more impressive plumage will be the male. Yeah, the green ones, yeah. That'll be the male.

questions.question: What is the difference between a road and a street?

answers.answer: Roads go places... Streets don't... So a street is a sort of collection of residential abodes and dwellings. A road is actually a thoroughfare that exists solely to get someone from A to B. Built by the Romans. But there's no roads in the square mile.

questions.question: If I wanted to wear a toupee, right, and I wanted to have the photo done, that was going to be my persona then, I was going to wear this toupee, would I have to remove it when I show my passport, or could you have that as part of your... as you might say. Are you allowed to wear your toupee and your passport picture?

answers.answer: Yes, you are. If it's part of what you would normally wear, then you are. Obviously, some people are follicly challenged after their passport photographs have been taken. So we often see people with all sorts of hairstyles that are not as they would be in the passport... As long as I'm the same person as the bald bloke in this. So there's no circumstances in which anyone would ever be asked to remove a hairpiece or a wig at customs? You're just checking that the person is as they appear. Or the person that's presenting is the person that's holding the passport. That's all you care about.

questions.question: Why is shortcrust pastry called shortcrust pastry?

answers.answer: You need to think of short as shallow and then you've got your answer... It's short as in depth, so it's short as in height. It's a short crust because it doesn't rise. It's pretty much the same thickness baked as it is unbaked, unlike a lot of other pastries, including choux or flaky or puff or probably phyllo.

Short cross pastry has nothing to do with the depth of pastry. It's the American's version of fat and margarine and butter. It's commonly known as shortening. And so it's a pastry made with shortening.

questions.question: When I was a little kid, I always remember my mum saying to me, oh, that man's gone grey with worry. Is there any truth that worrying makes your hair go grey?

answers.answer: My hair was going grey and then falling out, and my wife didn't mind it falling out, but she didn't like it going grey. So, she did all matters of research and came up with the fact that when you get stressed, you start to lose vitamins, but you also lose minerals. One of the most important minerals for your hair colour is copper. And you deplete yourself of copper. So, therefore, if you take copper, your hair won't go grey... I took copper. And it did, but my hair hasn't gone grey.

questions.question: When the world was created, it was all aflame. Everything was like a big giant volcano. If that was all on fire... The Earth's now covered with two-thirds of water. Where'd all that water come from?

answers.answer: It's a hydrogen and oxygen, isn't it? So, the gases react with each other... Some people think it's come via asteroids. Otherwise, it would just be a chemical reaction between hydrogen atoms and oxygen atoms.

What he said about where the water came from is the accepted theory. Asteroids, we're talking over millennia. Loads of asteroids crashing onto the planet, made up of ice, and eventually melting, turning into water. Although it's not proven, it is the accepted theory, according to your man, Brian Cobb.

questions.question: How much alcohol you can get away with without getting dehydrated? So, say you drink four pints, you've had four pints of water, but it's 4% alcohol, you're going to feel dehydrated. What's the minimum alcohol, or sorry, the maximum alcohol I can have without getting that dehydration? Is there any way you can enjoy a tipple without dehydrating?

answers.answer: A very good friend of mine, when I was a gossip columnist on the newspapers, who spent his life either hungover or drunk, always recommended diarrhea medication for rehydration.

Once you start drinking alcohol, the hormone released from the pituitary glands in the brain, antidiuretic hormone, is immediately suppressed, so that's why you pee more when you drink. Because the ADH hormone actually helps conserve your water in your body, but obviously alcohol suppresses that. So, actually, obviously the more you drink... So, any alcohol at all will suppress... Yeah, it will start to suppress the hormone.

questions.question: Do horses answer to their name like dogs do? I keep asking this question, and no one can tell me.

answers.answer: Yes, they do. They don't react to their show name... We've got one called his show name is Bell's Desert Kestrel. But the name we call him is Pixie because he's a naughty pixie and he likes to bite people. And if you shout Pixie, he comes across the field, and if you haven't got anything to give him to eat, he tries to bite you. And the crucial question here is, do the other four horses stay put? They do, unless you've got food in your hand, then it doesn't matter what you call them. They'll all come over if there's a feed, but you could almost pick them off one by one by name.

questions.question: How deep is the Thames at low tide between London Bridge and Tower Bridge? Could you walk across it?

answers.answer: At Chiswick you can walk to Oliver's Island at low tide, but not across to the far bank because it's deeper on the Barnes/Kew side. At Brentford there's a ford - that's why it's called Brentford (where Romans came in). Boats ground out at low tide.
At the source of the Thames you can step across it completely.

questions.question: Why don't we have any famous female classical composers like Mozart, Beethoven, etc.?

answers.answer: It was about financial support and patronage. Women were frowned upon for 'manly pursuits' like being a composer. A female couldn't get an orchestra to play anything she composed because it was unseemly, so she could never get recognition or improve her compositions.

Hildegard von Bingen (12th century German nun), Clara Schumann (wife of Robert Schumann), Fanny Mendelssohn Hensel. Their existence doesn't disprove the underrepresentation but their exemption from social conditions allowed them to write.

questions.question: Why does China have only one time zone when the USA has three?

answers.answer: China used to have different time zones but the government simplified it to improve efficiency of travelling, trains, and internal transportation. Probably post-revolution, possibly Mao Zedong's doing for uniformity of nationhood.

questions.question: What does the T stand for in 'Down to a T'?

answers.answer: It comes from the T-square, which carpenters and architects use to draw straight lines and angles. A T-square allows you to measure a perfect angle.
It comes from when tea was imported. The head taster would taste tea and say it was 'down to a tea' - abbreviation to tea.
T is actually from the biblical term T-I-T-T-L-E (tittle), a finite particle, the smallest discernible something. 'Tattle' became common in English in the 17th century, from Latin.

questions.question: How do blind people tell the difference between American banknotes when they're all the same size and have no Braille?

answers.answer: They fold it into different shapes so when pulling from wallet they know the denomination by the fold.
